title_en: Intensive parenting is no longer the preserve of the rich
excerpt_en: But wealthy families still come out on top

enrich.title_zh: 密集型育儿不再是有钱人的专属
enrich.summary_zh: 标题指出，密集型育儿已不再只是富裕家庭的专利；提要随即补充，富裕家庭仍然占据上风。两句话构成转折：参与这种育儿方式的家庭范围可能扩大，但阶层优势并未消失。

paragraphs.en: But wealthy families still come out on top
paragraphs.zh: 但富裕家庭仍然占据上风。

vocab.meaning_zh: 密集型育儿（指父母投入大量时间、精力与资源来培养孩子的育儿方式）
vocab.example_en: Intensive parenting often involves scheduled activities and close supervision.
vocab.example_zh: 密集型育儿通常包括安排好的活动和密切监督。

vocab.meaning_zh: 专属领域；专利（no longer the preserve of 表示“不再是……的专利”）
vocab.example_en: Chess was once the preserve of older men.
vocab.example_zh: 国际象棋曾经是年长男性的专属领域。

vocab.meaning_zh: 最终占上风；胜出；占据优势
vocab.example_en: Despite the new rules, the largest firms still came out on top.
vocab.example_zh: 尽管有新规定，最大的公司仍然占据优势。

sentences.en: But wealthy families still come out on top
sentences.structure: 主干：wealthy families（主语）+ come out on top（谓语短语）／修饰：But 为转折连词，still 为副词状语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一个简短有力的转折句。come out on top 是习语，意为“最终胜出、占上风”；still 强调前句所说的变化并没有改变结果。放在标题之后，形成“范围扩大—优势仍在”的张力。

background.title: 密集型育儿（intensive parenting）
background.text_zh: 密集型育儿是社会学术语，指父母在孩子身上投入大量时间、金钱和精力，包括安排结构化活动、辅导学习、密切参与孩子成长等。相关讨论常涉及社会阶层、教育竞争和资源不平等。这里只解释术语背景，不推断文章正文的具体论证。

title_en: Cryosphere faces permanent damage when world overshoots 1.5C, scientists warn
excerpt_en: UN-backed report finds even temporary rises above Paris agreement target could cause harm to glaciers and polar ice sheets
body_en: Earth’s icy regions face such dangerous melting that global heating should be brought back below 1C after an inevitable period of overshooting global temperature targets, a UN report has found.

Permanent and widespread losses of snow and ice expose a “persistent myth” that overshooting the 1.5C target of the Paris climate agreement – to 2C or 3C – could be manageable or even preferable to urgent cuts to emissions, the report found.

The planet has heated by 1.3C since pre-industrial times and failures to curb greenhouse gas emissions and protect nature have led scientists to conclude that some level of overshoot is inevitable as they fight to keep end-of-century warming to 1.5C.

But extreme effects on the cryosphere – Earth’s water in a solid state, including all its ice and snow – mean temperatures must rise above that threshold for as short a period as possible, the scientists urged. Added to this, enough planet-heating carbon should be removed from the atmosphere to bring long-term warming down much further, ideally below 1C by 2150.
Related: The threatening thaw: climate professor on heatwave risks to tipping point of permafrost

The high overshoot expected under current policies – with peak temperatures of about 3C – would thaw nearly all near-surface permafrost, make “severe and possibly abrupt” disruption to ocean circulation likely, and lead to widespread acidification, the report found. The latest scientific research suggests sea ice recovers more slowly than previously thought.

The report, written by 80 scientists brought together by the International Cryosphere Climate Initiative (ICCI) and the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), found much of the damage would be permanent even if global temperatures were brought back down to 1.5C, such as glacier melt raising sea levels and threatening water security.

James Kirkham, a glaciologist at ICCI and the lead author of the report, said the cryosphere is “one of the most sensitive components of the climate system”, and the consequences of its loss affect the whole planet.

“This year, we’ve already seen one of the largest and most deadly ice rock avalanches ever recorded, on the Nepal-China border – it killed thousands of people and left damage equivalent to 10% of Nepal’s GDP in a single event,” said Kirkham. “Switzerland has lost 20% of its glacier ice in the last five years, and thousands of glaciers worldwide are expected to become extinct in the coming decade, every single year.”

The report, which comes as world leaders and diplomats converge on Turkey for the 31st annual Cop climate conference, documented rapid and accelerating melting of the cryosphere and polar oceans, with damages that range from the loss of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets, driving sea level rises that threaten hundreds of millions of people, to thawing permafrost, which releases more planet-heating gas.

Glaciers, which are still responding to historical warming, would only preserve about 70% of their current volume over a timescale of centuries if long-term heating were brought back down to 0.8C, the report found.
Related: Slovenia mourns loss of glacier on its highest peak after scorching summer

Meanwhile, the ice sheets covering Greenland and Antarctica, which are melting about six times faster today than in the 1990s, would continue to lose ice even in scenarios where overshoot is brief and temperature rise returns to 1.5C, the report found. The scientists said a safe, long-term temperature limit for polar ice sheets lies much closer to 1.0C of global heating, and possibly even lower.

“Snow and ice respond rapidly to every fraction of a degree of warming,” said Kirkham. “But most of these systems will take centuries or millennia to recover after overshoot, especially if tipping points are crossed that cause changes to become essentially irreversible.”

Last month, a UNEP report found the world must cut emissions by 18% by 2030 and by 45% by 2035 to have a good chance of keeping temperatures from rising 1.7C above preindustrial levels. It found there were “no good outcomes” of remaining above 1.5C.

The cryosphere report found that current policies, which will result in 2.8C of global heating, would reduce the mass of glacier ice to below 10% in the Rockies, Alps, Iceland and Scandinavia. If warming was limited to 1.5C, about 20-35% of the mass would remain.

In the Hindu Kush Himalayas, where glaciers are a source of water for nearly a quarter of humanity, current policies will leave just 41% of the ice mass. If warming was limited to 1.5C, 83% would remain.

Bill Hare, a climate scientist and the CEO of Climate Analytics, a policy institute, who was not involved in the report, said: “Ice sheets melting six times faster than 30 years ago, sea ice and mountain glaciers disappearing at record speed, sea levels inexorably rising, the life-giving polar oceans acidifying: all irreversible now on human timescales, all laden with worldwide consequences, and all taking climate impacts past limits of adaptability.”

He added: “Every government minister and every fossil fuel executive who’s ever succeeded in watering down climate action can look at this report and see how their actions have fundamentally damaged the world we live in.”

enrich.title_zh: 科学家警告：一旦全球升温超标，冰冻圈将遭受永久性损害
enrich.summary_zh: 一份由联合国环境规划署与国际冰冻圈气候倡议组织召集 80 位科学家撰写的报告指出，地球冰雪区域对每一分之一的升温都极为敏感。即使日后把升温拉回 1.5°C，冰川消融、冰盖失冰、冻土解冻等大部分损害仍将永久存在，因此除尽快减排外，还需大规模移除碳，把长期升温降至 1°C 甚至更低。

paragraphs.en: Earth’s icy regions face such dangerous melting that global heating should be brought back below 1C after an inevitable period of overshooting global temperature targets, a UN report has found.
paragraphs.zh: 一份联合国报告发现，地球的冰冻区域正面临极其危险的融化，因此在不可避免的气温超标阶段之后，全球升温应被拉回到 1°C 以下。

paragraphs.en: Permanent and widespread losses of snow and ice expose a “persistent myth” that overshooting the 1.5C target of the Paris climate agreement – to 2C or 3C – could be manageable or even preferable to urgent cuts to emissions, the report found.
paragraphs.zh: 报告发现，积雪与冰层永久而大范围的流失，戳破了一个“长期流传的迷思”：即突破《巴黎气候协定》1.5°C 的目标、升至 2°C 或 3°C，是可以承受的，甚至比紧急减排更可取。

paragraphs.en: The planet has heated by 1.3C since pre-industrial times and failures to curb greenhouse gas emissions and protect nature have led scientists to conclude that some level of overshoot is inevitable as they fight to keep end-of-century warming to 1.5C.
paragraphs.zh: 自前工业化时代以来，地球已升温 1.3°C；由于未能遏制温室气体排放、也未能保护好自然，科学家们得出结论：在他们力争把本世纪末的升温控制在 1.5°C 的同时，某种程度的“超标”已不可避免。

paragraphs.en: But extreme effects on the cryosphere – Earth’s water in a solid state, including all its ice and snow – mean temperatures must rise above that threshold for as short a period as possible, the scientists urged. Added to this, enough planet-heating carbon should be removed from the atmosphere to bring long-term warming down much further, ideally below 1C by 2150.
paragraphs.zh: 但科学家们敦促说，对冰冻圈——即地球以固态形式存在的水，包括所有冰雪——的极端影响意味着，气温高于这一阈值的持续时间必须尽可能短。除此之外，还应从大气中移除足够多的致暖碳，使长期升温幅度进一步大幅下降，理想情况下到 2150 年降至 1°C 以下。

paragraphs.en: Related: The threatening thaw: climate professor on heatwave risks to tipping point of permafrost
paragraphs.zh: 相关阅读：《来势汹汹的解冻：气候学教授谈热浪给永久冻土临界点带来的风险》

paragraphs.en: The high overshoot expected under current policies – with peak temperatures of about 3C – would thaw nearly all near-surface permafrost, make “severe and possibly abrupt” disruption to ocean circulation likely, and lead to widespread acidification, the report found. The latest scientific research suggests sea ice recovers more slowly than previously thought.
paragraphs.zh: 报告发现，按现行政策预计会出现的大幅超标——峰值气温约 3°C——将融化几乎全部近地表永久冻土，使海洋环流很可能遭受“严重甚至可能是突发的”扰动，并导致大范围酸化。最新科学研究表明，海冰的恢复速度比人们此前认为的更慢。

paragraphs.en: The report, written by 80 scientists brought together by the International Cryosphere Climate Initiative (ICCI) and the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), found much of the damage would be permanent even if global temperatures were brought back down to 1.5C, such as glacier melt raising sea levels and threatening water security.
paragraphs.zh: 这份报告由国际冰冻圈气候倡议组织（ICCI）与联合国环境规划署（UNEP）召集的 80 位科学家撰写。报告发现，即便全球气温回落到 1.5°C，大部分损害仍将是永久性的，例如冰川融化推高海平面并威胁水资源安全。

paragraphs.en: James Kirkham, a glaciologist at ICCI and the lead author of the report, said the cryosphere is “one of the most sensitive components of the climate system”, and the consequences of its loss affect the whole planet.
paragraphs.zh: ICCI 冰川学家、该报告第一作者詹姆斯·柯克汉姆表示，冰冻圈是“气候系统中最敏感的组成部分之一”，其丧失带来的后果会影响整个星球。

paragraphs.en: “This year, we’ve already seen one of the largest and most deadly ice rock avalanches ever recorded, on the Nepal-China border – it killed thousands of people and left damage equivalent to 10% of Nepal’s GDP in a single event,” said Kirkham. “Switzerland has lost 20% of its glacier ice in the last five years, and thousands of glaciers worldwide are expected to become extinct in the coming decade, every single year.”
paragraphs.zh: 柯克汉姆说：“今年，我们已经在尼中边境看到了有记录以来规模最大、最致命的冰岩崩之一——它造成数千人死亡，单次事件造成的损失相当于尼泊尔 GDP 的 10%。”“瑞士在过去五年里失去了 20% 的冰川冰，而全球数以千计的冰川预计在未来十年里，每年都会有一批彻底消失。”

paragraphs.en: The report, which comes as world leaders and diplomats converge on Turkey for the 31st annual Cop climate conference, documented rapid and accelerating melting of the cryosphere and polar oceans, with damages that range from the loss of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets, driving sea level rises that threaten hundreds of millions of people, to thawing permafrost, which releases more planet-heating gas.
paragraphs.zh: 这份报告发布之际，世界各国领导人与外交官正齐聚土耳其参加第 31 届联合国气候变化大会（Cop）。报告记录了对冰冻圈与极地海洋迅速且不断加速的融化，其损害范围之广，从格陵兰与南极冰盖的消融——它推动海平面上升，威胁数亿人——到永久冻土解冻、进而释放更多致暖气体。

paragraphs.en: Glaciers, which are still responding to historical warming, would only preserve about 70% of their current volume over a timescale of centuries if long-term heating were brought back down to 0.8C, the report found.
paragraphs.zh: 报告发现，冰川至今仍在对历史累积的升温作出反应；即使长期升温被拉回 0.8°C，在数百年的尺度上，它们也只能保住目前体积的约 70%。

paragraphs.en: Related: Slovenia mourns loss of glacier on its highest peak after scorching summer
paragraphs.zh: 相关阅读：酷暑过后，斯洛文尼亚为其最高峰冰川的消失而哀痛

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the ice sheets covering Greenland and Antarctica, which are melting about six times faster today than in the 1990s, would continue to lose ice even in scenarios where overshoot is brief and temperature rise returns to 1.5C, the report found. The scientists said a safe, long-term temperature limit for polar ice sheets lies much closer to 1.0C of global heating, and possibly even lower.
paragraphs.zh: 报告发现，覆盖格陵兰与南极的冰盖如今的融化速度约为 1990 年代的六倍，即便在“超标时间短暂、升温回落到 1.5°C”的情景下，它们仍会继续失冰。科学家表示，对极地冰盖而言安全的长期温度上限要低得多，更接近 1.0°C，甚至可能更低。

paragraphs.en: “Snow and ice respond rapidly to every fraction of a degree of warming,” said Kirkham. “But most of these systems will take centuries or millennia to recover after overshoot, especially if tipping points are crossed that cause changes to become essentially irreversible.”
paragraphs.zh: 柯克汉姆说：“冰雪对每一分之一的升温都会迅速作出反应。”“但在超标之后，这些系统大多需要数百年乃至数千年才能恢复，尤其是当跨越临界点、使变化变得基本上不可逆转时。”

paragraphs.en: Last month, a UNEP report found the world must cut emissions by 18% by 2030 and by 45% by 2035 to have a good chance of keeping temperatures from rising 1.7C above preindustrial levels. It found there were “no good outcomes” of remaining above 1.5C.
paragraphs.zh: 上个月，环境署的一份报告发现，世界必须在 2030 年前减排 18%、2035 年前减排 45%，才有较大把握把升温控制在比前工业化水平高 1.7°C 以内。该报告认为，停留在 1.5°C 以上“不会有好结果”。

paragraphs.en: The cryosphere report found that current policies, which will result in 2.8C of global heating, would reduce the mass of glacier ice to below 10% in the Rockies, Alps, Iceland and Scandinavia. If warming was limited to 1.5C, about 20-35% of the mass would remain.
paragraphs.zh: 这份冰冻圈报告发现，现行政策将导致全球升温 2.8°C，这会使落基山脉、阿尔卑斯山、冰岛和斯堪的纳维亚的冰川冰量降至不足 10%。如果升温被限制在 1.5°C，则约有 20%–35% 的冰量得以保留。

paragraphs.en: In the Hindu Kush Himalayas, where glaciers are a source of water for nearly a quarter of humanity, current policies will leave just 41% of the ice mass. If warming was limited to 1.5C, 83% would remain.
paragraphs.zh: 在兴都库什—喜马拉雅地区，冰川是近四分之一人类的水源；按现行政策，那里将只剩 41% 的冰量。若升温被限制在 1.5°C，则可保留 83%。

paragraphs.en: Bill Hare, a climate scientist and the CEO of Climate Analytics, a policy institute, who was not involved in the report, said: “Ice sheets melting six times faster than 30 years ago, sea ice and mountain glaciers disappearing at record speed, sea levels inexorably rising, the life-giving polar oceans acidifying: all irreversible now on human timescales, all laden with worldwide consequences, and all taking climate impacts past limits of adaptability.”
paragraphs.zh: 气候科学家、政策研究机构“气候分析”（Climate Analytics）首席执行官比尔·黑尔未参与这份报告，他说：“冰盖的融化速度是 30 年前的六倍，海冰与高山冰川正以创纪录的速度消失，海平面不可阻挡地上升，孕育生命的极地海洋正在酸化：在人类的时间尺度上，这一切如今都已不可逆，都承载着全球性的后果，并且都在把气候影响推过可承受的极限。”

paragraphs.en: He added: “Every government minister and every fossil fuel executive who’s ever succeeded in watering down climate action can look at this report and see how their actions have fundamentally damaged the world we live in.”
paragraphs.zh: 他补充说：“每一位曾经成功削弱气候行动的政府部长和化石燃料企业高管，都可以看看这份报告，看看他们的所作所为是如何从根本上破坏了我们所生活的这个世界。”

vocab.meaning_zh: （升温等）超出目标、超标；冲过头。气候语境中特指气温暂时突破 1.5°C 后再回落
vocab.example_en: Even a brief overshoot of 1.5C risks permanent damage to polar ice.
vocab.example_zh: 即便只是短暂突破 1.5°C，也可能给极地冰盖带来永久性损害。

vocab.meaning_zh: 冰冻圈，即地球上以固态存在的水，包括冰盖、冰川、海冰、积雪和冻土
vocab.example_en: The cryosphere stores most of the planet's fresh water as ice and snow.
vocab.example_zh: 冰冻圈以冰雪形式储存着地球上大部分的淡水。

vocab.meaning_zh: 永久冻土，长期处于冰点以下、本不应融化的土层
vocab.example_en: Thawing permafrost releases methane and carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
vocab.example_zh: 解冻的永久冻土会向大气释放甲烷和二氧化碳。

vocab.meaning_zh: 临界点，跨越后系统会发生难以逆转的突变
vocab.example_en: Scientists fear the Amazon may be approaching a tipping point.
vocab.example_zh: 科学家担心亚马孙雨林可能正逼近一个临界点。

vocab.meaning_zh: 酸化（尤指海水吸收二氧化碳后酸性增强）
vocab.example_en: Ocean acidification is dissolving the shells of marine organisms.
vocab.example_zh: 海洋酸化正在溶解海洋生物的贝壳。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）稀释；引申为削弱、淡化（措辞、方案、行动力度）
vocab.example_en: The final text was watered down to win support from oil producers.
vocab.example_zh: 为争取产油国的支持，最终文本被打了折扣。

vocab.meaning_zh: 不可阻挡地、无可挽回地，强调趋势无法中止
vocab.example_en: Sea levels are rising inexorably as the ice sheets lose mass.
vocab.example_zh: 随着冰盖失冰，海平面正不可阻挡地上升。

vocab.meaning_zh: 满载着、承载着（多指沉重或负面之物）
vocab.example_en: The decision is laden with political consequences.
vocab.example_zh: 这一决定承载着沉重的政治后果。

vocab.meaning_zh: 突然的、急剧的；（变化）缺乏过渡的
vocab.example_en: An abrupt shift in ocean circulation would disrupt weather worldwide.
vocab.example_zh: 海洋环流的骤然变化会扰乱全球天气。

vocab.meaning_zh: 阈值、门槛值，超过即触发质变
vocab.example_en: Beyond a certain threshold, the damage becomes irreversible.
vocab.example_zh: 一旦超过某个阈值，损害就变得不可逆转。

sentences.en: Permanent and widespread losses of snow and ice expose a "persistent myth" that overshooting the 1.5C target of the Paris climate agreement – to 2C or 3C – could be manageable or even preferable to urgent cuts to emissions, the report found.
sentences.structure: 主干：losses expose a myth（主＋谓＋宾）。修饰：Permanent and widespread 作前置定语修饰 losses；that ... 引导同位语从句，说明 myth 的具体内容；从句主语是动名词短语 overshooting the 1.5C target，破折号中的 to 2C or 3C 是对 overshoot 程度的补充说明；从句谓语 could be manageable or even preferable to ...；句末 the report found 是后置的报道来源。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句的难点在于“宾语后置”：the report found 本应统领全句，却被放到句尾，让又长又重的同位语从句先出现，符合英语“尾重”原则，也让读者先看到最有冲击力的断言（永久流失戳破迷思）。翻译时宜先把 the report found 提到句首，再把 myth 的同位语从句用冒号或“即”引出。注意 expose a myth 是带有攻击性的评论性搭配，不是中性的“揭示”。

sentences.en: But extreme effects on the cryosphere – Earth's water in a solid state, including all its ice and snow – mean temperatures must rise above that threshold for as short a period as possible, the scientists urged. Added to this, enough planet-heating carbon should be removed from the atmosphere to bring long-term warming down much further, ideally below 1C by 2150.
sentences.structure: 第一句主干：effects mean (that) temperatures must rise（mean 后接省略 that 的宾语从句）；破折号之间是给 cryosphere 下定义的同位插入语；for as short a period as possible 作时间状语；the scientists urged 是后置的言说来源。第二句主干：carbon should be removed；Added to this 为句间连接语；不定式 to bring ... down 作目的状语，ideally below 1C by 2150 补充说明结果。
sentences.analysis_zh: 两句话构成“先止损、再回撤”的逻辑：第一句说超标期必须尽量短，第二句说光短还不够，还得靠碳移除把长期温度压得更低。作者用破折号插定义，是为了在不打断主句节奏的前提下照顾非专业读者；用 Added to this 而不是 Moreover，更口语、更像人在讲话。翻译时破折号内容可保留为插入语，但要保证“mean (that) ...”的宾语从句在中文里读得通顺。

sentences.en: Bill Hare, a climate scientist and the CEO of Climate Analytics, a policy institute, who was not involved in the report, said: "Ice sheets melting six times faster than 30 years ago, sea ice and mountain glaciers disappearing at record speed, sea levels inexorably rising, the life-giving polar oceans acidifying: all irreversible now on human timescales, all laden with worldwide consequences, and all taking climate impacts past limits of adaptability."
sentences.structure: 主句：Bill Hare said: “...”。修饰：a climate scientist and the CEO of Climate Analytics 是同位语，a policy institute 又为 Climate Analytics 作同位语，who was not involved in the report 是定语从句（说明其独立身份，增强可信度）。引语内部由冒号引出四个并列的“名词＋分词”结构（Ice sheets melting..., sea ice and mountain glaciers disappearing..., sea levels rising, oceans acidifying），均无谓语动词，属独立主格式的列举；随后三个 all 引导的短语收束总结。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是典型的英文“冒号＋平行排比”修辞：先四组画面式短语快速推进，制造压迫感，再用三个 all 结构把结论一次性砸下来，节奏由碎到整。翻译时宜保留冒号和排比，中文里可把独立主格译成小句或“的”字结构（“冰盖的融化……海平面的上升……”），三个 all 可处理成“这一切都已……都……都在……”，以维持气势。注意 who 从句在此不是限制性信息，删掉也不影响命题，但保留能体现受访者与报告的独立性。

background.title: “升温超标”（overshoot）到底在争什么
background.text_zh: 《巴黎协定》把“远低于 2°C、力争 1.5°C”写进文本，但现实中排放削减速度不够，多数模型情景只能假设“先冲高、后回落”：即本世纪内暂时突破 1.5°C，再依靠大规模碳移除把温度拉回来。支持者认为这比立刻激进减排更“经济可行”；批评者指出，碳移除技术尚未规模化，且温度回落并不等于系统恢复。这份报告正是从冰冻圈的角度加入这场争论：它把“暂时超标”从经济学假设问题，变成了物理上不可逆的损害问题。

background.title: 冰冻圈、临界点与 Cop
background.text_zh: 冰冻圈（cryosphere）是气候系统的一个组成部分，涵盖冰盖、山地冰川、海冰、积雪和永久冻土。它之所以被反复提及，是因为其中许多过程具有“临界点”性质：一旦跨过某个温度阈值，系统会自行加速变化，即使气温回落也难以复原，例如冰盖表面融化降低反照率、冻土解冻释放温室气体。文中的 ICCI（国际冰冻圈气候倡议组织）是一个专门把冰冻圈科学推向气候谈判桌的机构。Cop 指《联合国气候变化框架公约》缔约方大会，每年一届，是各国谈判气候行动的主要场合；本文提到第 31 届在土耳其举行。

title_en: Is the government really on an ‘out-of-control’ spending splurge? It’s complicated
excerpt_en: Defence, the NDIS and health responsible for much of increased government outlays and treasurer Jim Chalmers has few levers to pull
body_en: “Will the prime minister acknowledge reality … and admit Labor’s out-of-control spending is forcing families and small businesses to pay more for everything?”
That was the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, kicking off parliamentary question time on Wednesday.
Official data earlier that day showed inflation jumped to 4.3% in the year to September, from 4% the month before. Rapid petrol and diesel price increases drove that high headline figure.
But, even removing the impact of soaring fuel prices, underlying inflation ticked higher to 3.7% by the quarterly measure.
Both measures are way above the Reserve Bank’s 2.5% target – and a fifth interest rate hike on Tuesday looks like a done deal.
Frustrated Australians are increasingly inclined to believe Taylor’s argument.
So how much has government spending been rising? Should we blame climbing public expenditure for the cost of living crisis? And what should the government do about it?
Is the government spending more? The simple answer is: yes.
This is not surprising as you would expect the government to grow larger alongside the economy and the population.
But, leaving out the extraordinary payments associated with the Covid-19 pandemic, spending has been climbing at an unusually fast pace.
Total government expenses have jumped by 30% between 2021-22 and 2025-26, according to the parliamentary budget office.
Interactive Even after accounting for inflation, federal spending increased by 5.5% in 2024-25, and by 4.3% in 2025-26.
Stephen Bartos, a University of Canberra professor and a former deputy secretary at the finance department, says there are three key drivers of growing public outlays.
The first is defence, amid pressure on governments around the world to respond to an increasingly fraught geopolitical reality.
The second is the national disability insurance scheme (NDIS). Bartos says it would be a “herculean task” for the government to successfully halve growth in the scheme to 6% a year.
Related: Jim Chalmers is blaming Australia’s accelerating inflation on Trump – but voters aren’t buying it
“That is still twice as fast as the economy is growing,” he says.
“It ratcheted up considerably through Covid but never really came down.”
A more generous pharmaceutical benefits scheme and budgeting for new hospital funding deals with the states were part of the continuing rise in health spending.
Meanwhile, spending on the care economy beyond the NDIS was also climbing rapidly, as was paying interest on our expanding national debt.
Public expenditure as a share of the economy is now at its highest since the early 1980s – leaving out the pandemic period.
Interactive But Stephen Smith, a partner at Deloitte Access Economics, argues rising spending would have happened regardless of who held government.

enrich.title_zh: 政府真的在“失控”地大手大脚花钱吗？没那么简单
enrich.summary_zh: 澳大利亚通胀升至4.3%，反对党指责工党政府“支出失控”推高物价。文章核查数据后发现：即便剔除疫情支出和通胀影响，联邦支出仍在快速增长，主因是国防、全国残障保险计划、医疗卫生和国债利息，公共支出占经济比重已达上世纪80年代初以来最高。但德勤经济学家认为，支出扩张与哪个党执政关系不大。

paragraphs.en: “Will the prime minister acknowledge reality … and admit Labor’s out-of-control spending is forcing families and small businesses to pay more for everything?”
paragraphs.zh: “总理是否愿意承认现实……承认工党失控的支出正迫使家庭和小企业为一切东西付更多的钱？”

paragraphs.en: That was the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, kicking off parliamentary question time on Wednesday.
paragraphs.zh: 这是反对党领袖安格斯·泰勒周三在议会质询时间开场时说的话。

paragraphs.en: Official data earlier that day showed inflation jumped to 4.3% in the year to September, from 4% the month before. Rapid petrol and diesel price increases drove that high headline figure.
paragraphs.zh: 当天早些时候公布的官方数据显示，截至9月的一年内通胀率跃升至4.3%，高于上月的4%。汽油和柴油价格的快速上涨推高了这一整体（ headline ）数字。

paragraphs.en: But, even removing the impact of soaring fuel prices, underlying inflation ticked higher to 3.7% by the quarterly measure.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，即使剔除燃油价格飙升的影响，按季度衡量的核心通胀率仍小幅升至3.7%。

paragraphs.en: Both measures are way above the Reserve Bank’s 2.5% target – and a fifth interest rate hike on Tuesday looks like a done deal.
paragraphs.zh: 这两项指标都远高于澳大利亚储备银行2.5%的目标——而周二的第五次加息看起来已成定局。

paragraphs.en: Frustrated Australians are increasingly inclined to believe Taylor’s argument.
paragraphs.zh: 感到沮丧的澳大利亚人越来越倾向于相信泰勒的说法。

paragraphs.en: So how much has government spending been rising? Should we blame climbing public expenditure for the cost of living crisis? And what should the government do about it?
paragraphs.zh: 那么，政府支出到底涨了多少？我们该把生活成本危机归咎于不断攀升的公共支出吗？政府又该对此做些什么？

paragraphs.en: Is the government spending more? The simple answer is: yes.
paragraphs.zh: 政府花得更多了吗？简单的答案是：是的。

paragraphs.en: This is not surprising as you would expect the government to grow larger alongside the economy and the population.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不奇怪，因为政府本来就会随着经济规模和人口的增长而扩大。

paragraphs.en: But, leaving out the extraordinary payments associated with the Covid-19 pandemic, spending has been climbing at an unusually fast pace.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，如果抛开与新冠疫情相关的非常规支出，支出的攀升速度仍然异常之快。

paragraphs.en: Total government expenses have jumped by 30% between 2021-22 and 2025-26, according to the parliamentary budget office.
paragraphs.zh: 根据议会预算办公室的数据，政府总支出在2021-22财年到2025-26财年之间跃升了30%。

paragraphs.en: Interactive Even after accounting for inflation, federal spending increased by 5.5% in 2024-25, and by 4.3% in 2025-26.
paragraphs.zh: 即使把通胀因素考虑在内，联邦支出在2024-25财年仍增长了5.5%，在2025-26财年增长了4.3%。

paragraphs.en: Stephen Bartos, a University of Canberra professor and a former deputy secretary at the finance department, says there are three key drivers of growing public outlays.
paragraphs.zh: 堪培拉大学教授、财政部前副部长斯蒂芬·巴托斯认为，公共支出增长有三大关键推手。

paragraphs.en: The first is defence, amid pressure on governments around the world to respond to an increasingly fraught geopolitical reality.
paragraphs.zh: 第一是国防——世界各国政府都面临压力，要应对日益严峻的地缘政治现实。

paragraphs.en: The second is the national disability insurance scheme (NDIS). Bartos says it would be a “herculean task” for the government to successfully halve growth in the scheme to 6% a year.
paragraphs.zh: 第二是全国残障保险计划（NDIS）。巴托斯说，政府要想成功把该计划的增速减半、降到每年6%，将是一项“极其艰巨的任务”。

paragraphs.en: Related: Jim Chalmers is blaming Australia’s accelerating inflation on Trump – but voters aren’t buying it
paragraphs.zh: 相关阅读：吉姆·查默斯把澳大利亚加速的通胀归咎于特朗普——但选民并不买账

paragraphs.en: “That is still twice as fast as the economy is growing,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “这仍然是经济增长速度的两倍，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “It ratcheted up considerably through Covid but never really came down.”
paragraphs.zh: “它在疫情期间大幅抬升，之后就再没真正降下来。”

paragraphs.en: A more generous pharmaceutical benefits scheme and budgeting for new hospital funding deals with the states were part of the continuing rise in health spending.
paragraphs.zh: 更慷慨的药品福利计划（PBS），以及为与各州达成的新医院拨款协议预留预算，都是医疗支出持续上升的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, spending on the care economy beyond the NDIS was also climbing rapidly, as was paying interest on our expanding national debt.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，NDIS之外的照护经济支出也在快速攀升，为不断膨胀的国债支付利息同样如此。

paragraphs.en: Public expenditure as a share of the economy is now at its highest since the early 1980s – leaving out the pandemic period.
paragraphs.zh: 剔除疫情期间，公共支出占经济的比重现在已达到上世纪80年代初以来的最高水平。

paragraphs.en: Interactive But Stephen Smith, a partner at Deloitte Access Economics, argues rising spending would have happened regardless of who held government.
paragraphs.zh: 但德勤经济研究所合伙人斯蒂芬·史密斯认为，无论哪个党执政，支出上升都会发生。

vocab.meaning_zh: 挥霍，大手大脚地花钱（标题中指政府“乱花钱”）
vocab.example_en: Critics called the stimulus package a spending splurge.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者称这项刺激方案是挥霍性支出。

vocab.meaning_zh: 失控的，无法遏制的
vocab.example_en: He blamed out-of-control costs for the closure of the plant.
vocab.example_zh: 他把工厂关停归咎于失控的成本。

vocab.meaning_zh: 小幅上升、微升（财经报道高频搭配，另有 tick up / tick down）
vocab.example_en: Core prices ticked higher again last quarter.
vocab.example_zh: 上季度核心价格再度小幅走高。

vocab.meaning_zh: 核心通胀（剔除燃油、蔬果等波动较大项目后的通胀）
vocab.example_en: Underlying inflation is a better guide to price pressures than the headline rate.
vocab.example_zh: 相比整体通胀率，核心通胀更能反映价格压力。

vocab.meaning_zh: 已成定局的事，板上钉钉
vocab.example_en: After the latest data, another rate rise is a done deal.
vocab.example_zh: 最新数据出炉后，再次加息已成定局。

vocab.meaning_zh: （一笔）支出、开支，常指政府或机构的大额花费
vocab.example_en: Defence outlays will rise sharply over the next decade.
vocab.example_zh: 未来十年国防开支将大幅上升。

vocab.meaning_zh: 充满风险的，令人忧虑的（fraught 后常接 with）
vocab.example_en: The negotiations took place in a fraught political climate.
vocab.example_zh: 谈判在紧张的政治氛围中进行。

vocab.meaning_zh: 极其艰巨的，需付出巨大努力的（源自大力神 Hercules）
vocab.example_en: Cutting the deficit by half in two years would be a herculean task.
vocab.example_zh: 要在两年内将赤字减半将是极其艰巨的任务。

vocab.meaning_zh: （一步步地）抬高、递增，且往往难以回落
vocab.example_en: Costs ratcheted up during the boom and never fell back.
vocab.example_zh: 成本在繁荣期节节攀升，之后再未回落。

vocab.meaning_zh: 照护经济，指围绕养老、托幼、残障照护等提供有偿或无偿照护服务的经济部门
vocab.example_en: The care economy is one of the fastest-growing sources of jobs.
vocab.example_zh: 照护经济是就业增长最快的领域之一。

sentences.en: “Will the prime minister acknowledge reality … and admit Labor’s out-of-control spending is forcing families and small businesses to pay more for everything?”
sentences.structure: 主干：Will the prime minister acknowledge … and admit …?（两个并列谓语共用一个主语）；宾语：admit 后接省略 that 的宾语从句 Labor’s out-of-control spending is forcing families and small businesses to pay more for everything；从句内部为 force sb to do sth 结构。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一句典型的议会攻击式问句：以情态动词 Will 开头，把“承认现实”和“承认工党乱花钱”并列起来，逼对方在二者间表态，无论怎么回答都陷于被动。省略号处的停顿是口语化的施压节奏，宾语从句里用 force sb to do sth 把“支出”与“家庭、小企业付更多钱”直接画上因果等号——这是一种修辞指控，而非已证实的结论，后文正是要检验这个因果链条。

sentences.en: Both measures are way above the Reserve Bank’s 2.5% target – and a fifth interest rate hike on Tuesday looks like a done deal.
sentences.structure: 主干：Both measures are above the target；破折号后用 and 连接第二个并列分句，主语 a fifth interest rate hike，谓语 looks like，宾语 a done deal；on Tuesday 为时间状语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子先用 way（口语化的程度副词，相当于 far）强调偏离幅度，再用破折号把“通胀超标”推进到“必然加息”的后果上，完成从数据到政策含义的跳转。looks like a done deal 是记者留有余地的判断句式：既表达高度确信，又避免直接断言。

sentences.en: A more generous pharmaceutical benefits scheme and budgeting for new hospital funding deals with the states were part of the continuing rise in health spending.
sentences.structure: 主干：A more generous pharmaceutical benefits scheme and budgeting … were part of the continuing rise；主语为 and 连接的两个并列名词短语（第二个是动名词 budgeting for … deals with the states），谓语用复数 were。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是外刊常见的“重主语”句式：主语长达十几个词，谓语被推到句子后部，读者要读到 were 才反应过来。理解的关键是先切分并列主语——一是“更慷慨的药品福利计划”，二是“为新医院拨款协议预留预算”，二者都是医疗支出上升的组成部分；deals with the states 是修饰 funding 的后置成分，不是谓语动词。

background.title: 议会质询时间（Question Time）
background.text_zh: 澳大利亚联邦议会众议院开会期间的固定环节：反对党议员可以当面向总理及各部部长提问，执政党议员也可提问。该环节火药味最浓，反对党领袖的首次提问通常成为当晚新闻的标题句，因此本文开篇引用的正是这一句。它属于政治表演与问责机制的结合体，提问往往带有预设结论，未必是中立提问。

background.title: NDIS 与 PBS：澳大利亚两项“大钱”制度
background.text_zh: 全国残障保险计划（NDIS）于2013年起逐步推行，为永久性或严重残障人士提供个性化资助，是联邦预算中增长最快的项目之一，其增速与成本控制长期是政治争议焦点。药品福利计划（PBS）则是政府补贴处方药的制度，政府通过谈判确定补贴范围与价格；所谓“更慷慨”通常指扩大补贴药品种类或降低患者自付额，都会推高财政支出。此外，澳大利亚的通胀目标由储备银行与政府约定为2%–3%区间，政策沟通中常以2.5%作为中点。

title_en: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda
excerpt_en: British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda
body_en: British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.

Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the reparatory justice movement Repair Campaign, welcomed Britain’s decision to enter structured dialogue on reparations, but said the UK had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.
Currently, slavery reparations is not on the official agenda of the Commonwealth Heads of Government (Chogm) summit, which begins on Sunday.

Trade, climate resilience and finance, sustainable debt, democracy and investment in opportunities for young people are among the stated priorities for the 56-nation bloc spanning Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and the Americas, the Pacific and Europe.

“My understanding from informed circles is that Britain was vehement not to have the matter on the agenda. The British officials – and in that regard they were joined by the Canadian officials – were even raising the prospect that if it is on the agenda the prime minister of Britain wouldn’t go,” Gonsalves told the Guardian.

“They also started to circulate this untruth that India didn’t want it on the agenda, but that was not so at all. India was very supportive at the UN general assembly resolution on March 25th, 2026. So they were spreading this false word about India.”

Gonsalves said that the relentless campaign by Caribbean nations, amplified by a growing regional and global reparations movement, has propelled reparatory justice to the heart of the political conversation at the meeting.

“Because of what happened at the UN, because of what happened in Africa, what happened in the Caribbean, and all the work which is taking place in Britain itself too, inside of the British parliament, inside of the British Labour party, both in the Commons and the House of Lords, it is an issue which you can’t duck any more,” he said.

He added: “The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda is what we see happening now, that everybody who could have foreseen, whether or not it’s formally on the agenda, even the nature of how the discussions take place at the Commonwealth, and certainly in the retreats, it would have been raised.”

Gonsalves said while the actual structured dialoguewas unlikely to happen at Chogm, it was expected that when the leaders met in their private retreat, the format and details of the dialogue would be discussed.
He said: “The British government, they’re coming, kicking and screaming to the table of structured dialogue. But at least they’re coming.”

An FCDO spokesperson said: “We categorically reject this completely untrue accusation. The UK has approached this conversation in good faith, and we have at no point told any other Chogm member what should not be on an agenda.
“Our position on reparations is clear but this government respects the right of others to raise matters as they wish.”
Related: ‘We want a full apology for slavery’: Commonwealth at a crossroads as king heads to the Caribbean

Prof Sir Hilary Beckles, chair of the Caribbean Community (Caricom) Reparations Commission, had described the meeting as “the Chogm of reparations”, adding that reparatory justice was “the number one item” for the Caribbean as Commonwealth leaders gather in the region.
On Friday there was a historic shift in Britain’s position when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors by agreeing to structured dialogue and to consider an apology.

Though Caribbean governments and campaigners welcomed Burnham’s announcement, made in an op-ed for the Guardian, it was clear that agreeing on forms of reparations was still a priority for the region.
Guyana’s president, Irfaan Ali, welcomed Burnham’s statement and called for a Commonwealth subcommittee to work out the details of the dialogue over the next six to 12 months.
“I’m happy that finally the discourse has moved to a position where it should have been, where the British government is involved, because that’s the state we are dealing with,” he said.
Ali said the talks should move beyond attempting to put a price on the indignity of slavery and towards addressing its developmental consequences.

“How do we identify a system of support where the UK government, with its financial institutions, can sit with countries … and work on a development pathway, identify development gaps, whether in health, education, social services, infrastructure?”

Barbados’s prime minister, Mia Mottley, thanked Burnham for “breaking new ground”, while making clear that the two sides remained divided. “On reparations in particular, our views differ, and we will say so plainly and respectfully,” she said.

enrich.title_zh: 英国“激烈反对”将奴隶制赔偿列入英联邦峰会议程
enrich.summary_zh: 报道称，在安提瓜和巴布达举行的英联邦峰会前，英国官员强烈反对把奴隶制赔偿列入正式议程，甚至暗示首相伯纳姆可能因此缺席；加勒比政治人物冈萨尔维斯批评英方“又踢又叫”才肯对话，并指责英方散布印度反对该议题的假消息。英国外交部否认相关指控。伯纳姆已同意开启结构性对话并考虑道歉，加勒比领导人则要求把赔偿落到发展议题上。

paragraphs.en: British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.
paragraphs.zh: 据加勒比一位重要政治人物透露，英国官员据称坚持认为，有关奴隶制赔偿的讨论不应被列入在安提瓜和巴布达举行的英联邦领导人峰会议程，甚至警告说，如果这一议题被正式列入，安迪·伯纳姆将不出席会议。

paragraphs.en: Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the reparatory justice movement Repair Campaign, welcomed Britain’s decision to enter structured dialogue on reparations, but said the UK had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 拉尔夫·冈萨尔维斯是圣文森特和格林纳丁斯前总理，也是赔偿正义运动“赔偿运动”（Repair Campaign）的重要人物。他对英国决定就赔偿问题进入结构性对话表示欢迎，但表示英国是“又踢又叫”、极不情愿地才来到这场对话的。

paragraphs.en: Currently, slavery reparations is not on the official agenda of the Commonwealth Heads of Government (Chogm) summit, which begins on Sunday.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，奴隶制赔偿并未被列入将于周日开幕的英联邦政府首脑会议（Chogm）的正式议程。

paragraphs.en: Trade, climate resilience and finance, sustainable debt, democracy and investment in opportunities for young people are among the stated priorities for the 56-nation bloc spanning Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and the Americas, the Pacific and Europe.
paragraphs.zh: 这个横跨非洲、亚洲、加勒比和美洲、太平洋与欧洲的56国集团，对外公布的优先议题包括贸易、气候韧性与金融、可持续债务、民主，以及为年轻人创造机会的投资。

paragraphs.en: “My understanding from informed circles is that Britain was vehement not to have the matter on the agenda. The British officials – and in that regard they were joined by the Canadian officials – were even raising the prospect that if it is on the agenda the prime minister of Britain wouldn’t go,” Gonsalves told the Guardian.
paragraphs.zh: “我从消息灵通人士那里了解到的情况是，英国激烈反对把这件事列入议程。英国官员——在这一点上加拿大官员与他们站在一起——甚至提出了一种可能：如果它被列入议程，英国首相就不会出席，”冈萨尔维斯对《卫报》说。

paragraphs.en: “They also started to circulate this untruth that India didn’t want it on the agenda, but that was not so at all. India was very supportive at the UN general assembly resolution on March 25th, 2026. So they were spreading this false word about India.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们随后又开始散布一个不实说法，说印度不希望把它列入议程，但事实完全不是这样。在2026年3月25日的联合国大会决议上，印度是非常支持的。所以他们是在散布关于印度的假消息。”

paragraphs.en: Gonsalves said that the relentless campaign by Caribbean nations, amplified by a growing regional and global reparations movement, has propelled reparatory justice to the heart of the political conversation at the meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 冈萨尔维斯说，加勒比国家坚持不懈的争取，加上日益壮大的地区与全球赔偿运动的助推，已把赔偿正义推到了此次会议政治讨论的中心。

paragraphs.en: “Because of what happened at the UN, because of what happened in Africa, what happened in the Caribbean, and all the work which is taking place in Britain itself too, inside of the British parliament, inside of the British Labour party, both in the Commons and the House of Lords, it is an issue which you can’t duck any more,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “因为联合国发生的事，因为非洲发生的事，加勒比发生的事，也因为英国国内正在进行的种种工作——在英国议会内部、在英国工党内部，在下议院和上议院——这已经是一个你再也无法回避的问题，”他说。

paragraphs.en: He added: “The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda is what we see happening now, that everybody who could have foreseen, whether or not it’s formally on the agenda, even the nature of how the discussions take place at the Commonwealth, and certainly in the retreats, it would have been raised.”
paragraphs.zh: 他补充说：“不把它正式列入议程的危险，正是我们现在看到的情况：所有本可以预见这一点的人——无论它是否被正式列入议程，甚至讨论在英联邦内部以何种方式进行，尤其是在闭门务虚会上——本来都会把它提出来。”

paragraphs.en: Gonsalves said while the actual structured dialoguewas unlikely to happen at Chogm, it was expected that when the leaders met in their private retreat, the format and details of the dialogue would be discussed.
paragraphs.zh: 冈萨尔维斯说，虽然真正的结构性对话不太可能在英联邦政府首脑会议期间举行，但预计当领导人们在闭门务虚会上会面时，会讨论对话的形式和细节。

paragraphs.en: He said: “The British government, they’re coming, kicking and screaming to the table of structured dialogue. But at least they’re coming.”
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“英国政府是又踢又叫地来到结构性对话的谈判桌前的。但至少他们来了。”

paragraphs.en: An FCDO spokesperson said: “We categorically reject this completely untrue accusation. The UK has approached this conversation in good faith, and we have at no point told any other Chogm member what should not be on an agenda.
paragraphs.zh: 英国外交、联邦和发展事务部（FCDO）的一位发言人说：“我们坚决否认这一完全不实的指控。英国是以诚意对待这场对话的，我们从未在任何时候告诉任何其他英联邦政府首脑会议成员什么不应被列入议程。

paragraphs.en: “Our position on reparations is clear but this government respects the right of others to raise matters as they wish.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们在赔偿问题上的立场是明确的，但本届政府尊重其他国家按自己意愿提出议题的权利。”

paragraphs.en: Related: ‘We want a full apology for slavery’: Commonwealth at a crossroads as king heads to the Caribbean
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：“我们要求为奴隶制正式道歉”：国王前往加勒比之际，英联邦站在十字路口

paragraphs.en: Prof Sir Hilary Beckles, chair of the Caribbean Community (Caricom) Reparations Commission, had described the meeting as “the Chogm of reparations”, adding that reparatory justice was “the number one item” for the Caribbean as Commonwealth leaders gather in the region.
paragraphs.zh: 加勒比共同体（Caricom）赔偿委员会主席希拉里·贝克尔斯爵士教授曾把这次会议形容为“赔偿问题的英联邦峰会”，并称随着英联邦领导人齐聚该地区，赔偿正义是加勒比的“头号议题”。

paragraphs.en: On Friday there was a historic shift in Britain’s position when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors by agreeing to structured dialogue and to consider an apology.
paragraphs.zh: 周五，英国的立场发生了历史性转变：英国首相比任何一位前任都走得更远，同意进行结构性对话并考虑道歉。

paragraphs.en: Though Caribbean governments and campaigners welcomed Burnham’s announcement, made in an op-ed for the Guardian, it was clear that agreeing on forms of reparations was still a priority for the region.
paragraphs.zh: 伯纳姆在《卫报》评论版发表文章中作出这一宣布，加勒比各国政府和活动人士虽对此表示欢迎，但显然，就赔偿形式达成一致仍是该地区的优先事项。

paragraphs.en: Guyana’s president, Irfaan Ali, welcomed Burnham’s statement and called for a Commonwealth subcommittee to work out the details of the dialogue over the next six to 12 months.
paragraphs.zh: 圭亚那总统伊尔凡·阿里对伯纳姆的表态表示欢迎，并呼吁成立一个英联邦小组委员会，在未来6到12个月内拟定这场对话的具体细节。

paragraphs.en: “I’m happy that finally the discourse has moved to a position where it should have been, where the British government is involved, because that’s the state we are dealing with,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “我很高兴，讨论终于回到了它本该在的位置，也就是英国政府参与其中，因为这才是我们要打交道的对象，”他说。

paragraphs.en: Ali said the talks should move beyond attempting to put a price on the indignity of slavery and towards addressing its developmental consequences.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里说，谈判应超越试图为奴隶制带来的屈辱标价的做法，转而着手处理它在发展层面造成的后果。

paragraphs.en: “How do we identify a system of support where the UK government, with its financial institutions, can sit with countries … and work on a development pathway, identify development gaps, whether in health, education, social services, infrastructure?”
paragraphs.zh: “我们如何建立一个支持体系，让英国政府连同其金融机构能够与各国坐在一起……共同规划一条发展路径，找出发展缺口——无论是在卫生、教育、社会服务还是基础设施方面？”

paragraphs.en: Barbados’s prime minister, Mia Mottley, thanked Burnham for “breaking new ground”, while making clear that the two sides remained divided. “On reparations in particular, our views differ, and we will say so plainly and respectfully,” she said.
paragraphs.zh: 巴巴多斯总理米娅·莫特利感谢伯纳姆“开辟了新天地”，同时明确表示双方仍存在分歧。“特别是在赔偿问题上，我们的看法不同，我们会坦率而有礼貌地把这一点说出来，”她说。

vocab.meaning_zh: （历史上不义行为造成的）赔款、赔偿；此处特指对奴隶制历史罪行的赔偿
vocab.example_en: Caribbean nations have long demanded reparations for centuries of slavery.
vocab.example_zh: 加勒比国家长期以来一直要求为数百年的奴隶制提供赔偿。

vocab.meaning_zh: （态度、反对）激烈的、强烈的、坚决的
vocab.example_en: Britain was vehement that the issue should not appear on the agenda.
vocab.example_zh: 英国激烈反对把该议题列入议程。

vocab.meaning_zh: 又踢又叫；极不情愿地、被逼无奈地（做某事）
vocab.example_en: He was dragged into the reform kicking and screaming.
vocab.example_zh: 他是被逼无奈才被拖入这场改革的。

vocab.meaning_zh: 集团、阵营（由若干国家或团体组成的联合体）
vocab.example_en: The 56-nation bloc meets every two years.
vocab.example_zh: 这个由56个国家组成的集团每两年举行一次会议。

vocab.meaning_zh: 散布、传播（消息、说法），此处含贬义
vocab.example_en: They began to circulate a false story about India's position.
vocab.example_zh: 他们开始散布关于印度立场的不实说法。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）回避、躲避、推卸（责任或问题）
vocab.example_en: This is an issue the government can no longer duck.
vocab.example_zh: 这是政府再也无法回避的问题。

vocab.meaning_zh: （僻义）闭门务虚会、避静会；领导人私下不对外的小范围聚谈
vocab.example_en: The leaders will discuss the format in their private retreat.
vocab.example_zh: 领导人将在闭门务虚会上讨论这一形式。

vocab.meaning_zh: 放大、增强、助推（声音、影响、声势）
vocab.example_en: Social media amplified the campaign's message.
vocab.example_zh: 社交媒体放大了这场运动的声音。

vocab.meaning_zh: （报纸的）评论版文章、特约评论稿（opposite the editorial page 的缩略）
vocab.example_en: He made the announcement in an op-ed for the Guardian.
vocab.example_zh: 他在《卫报》的一篇评论文章中宣布了这一消息。

vocab.meaning_zh: 开辟新天地、有所突破、开创新局面
vocab.example_en: She thanked him for breaking new ground on the issue.
vocab.example_zh: 她感谢他在这一问题上打开了新局面。

sentences.en: British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.
sentences.structure: 主干：British officials insisted ... and even warned ...（两个并列谓语）｜宾语从句1：that discussions ... should not be on the agenda of ... summit；宾语从句2：that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting；条件状语从句：if the subject was formally included；插入成分：reportedly（据称）、according to a leading Caribbean political figure（据一位加勒比重要政治人物说）
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一句典型的新闻导语句：先用 reportedly 和句末的 according to 双重标注消息来源，表明“指控”性质而非本报定论——这是英文媒体规避法律风险的常规手法。两个 that 从句由 insisted 和 warned 并列带出，层层递进：先“反对列入议程”，再“威胁首相缺席”。中文习惯把消息来源前置（“据……透露”），英文则常后置，翻译时需要调整语序。

sentences.en: “The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda is what we see happening now, that everybody who could have foreseen, whether or not it’s formally on the agenda, even the nature of how the discussions take place at the Commonwealth, and certainly in the retreats, it would have been raised.”
sentences.structure: 主干：The danger ... is what we see happening now｜主语：The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda（介词短语作后置定语）｜表语从句：what we see happening now｜that 引导的同位语从句解释 danger 的具体内容：everybody ... it would have been raised（口语中重复主语 everybody，是典型的口语冗赘结构）｜插入成分：whether or not it's formally on the agenda / even the nature of how the discussions take place / and certainly in the retreats
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是直接引语，保留了说话人现场组织语言时的重复与断裂，因此语法上并不“干净”：that 从句里 everybody 出现后又被 it would have been raised 重新起头，形成主语悬置。理解的关键是先抓住骨架“不列入议程的危险＝我们现在看到的局面”，其余都是插入的让步与补充。翻译时不必复制这种破碎感，可把插入成分用破折号括起来，保证中文可读。

sentences.en: On Friday there was a historic shift in Britain’s position when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors by agreeing to structured dialogue and to consider an apology.
sentences.structure: 主干：there was a historic shift（there be 句型）｜时间状语：On Friday｜后置定语：in Britain's position｜时间状语从句：when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors｜方式状语：by agreeing to structured dialogue and to consider an apology（两个 to 并列，第二个 to 后接动词原形 consider）
sentences.analysis_zh: 用 there was a historic shift 把“变化”本身置于主语位置，是外刊写转折的常用套路：先给判断（历史性转变），再给事实（首相的表态）。went further than any of his predecessors 是评价性的比较结构，暗含“历任首相都没走到这一步”。by agreeing to ... and to consider ... 中两个不定式并列，注意第二个 to 不是介词而是不定式符号。

background.title: 英联邦与 Chogm
background.text_zh: 英联邦（the Commonwealth）是由英国及其前殖民地、自治领组成的政府间组织，现有56个成员国，秘书处设在伦敦，元首名义上为英国国王。Chogm 即 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting（英联邦政府首脑会议），通常每两年举行一次，会后发表公报；领导人还会举行不对外公开的“retreat（闭门务虚会）”，许多敏感议题往往在那里谈，而不写进正式议程。本次会议在加勒比岛国安提瓜和巴布达举行，因此赔偿议题被推到台前。

background.title: 奴隶制赔偿与 Caricom 十点计划
background.text_zh: 加勒比共同体（Caricom）2003年成立赔偿委员会，2014年提出对前殖民宗主国（主要是英国、法国、荷兰）的“十点赔偿计划”，内容包括正式道歉、债务减免、发展援助、公共卫生与教育投入、文化机构归还等，并明确拒绝“只道歉不谈实质”的做法。2013年成立的 Repair Campaign 是推动该议题的重要民间运动。争论焦点之一是：赔偿是否应“定价”，还是应转向弥补奴隶制造成的长期发展差距——这正是文中圭亚那总统阿里主张的方向。

title_en: Top Trump Officials Are Hitting the Campaign Trail Ahead of the Midterms. Are They Allowed To?
excerpt_en: Legal experts and advocacy groups contend that in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms, members of the Administration have violated a decades-old law.

enrich.title_zh: 特朗普政府高官在中期选举前奔波助选，这样做合法吗？
enrich.summary_zh: 距离美国中期选举还有一段时间，特朗普政府的高层官员已频繁出现在竞选活动现场，为共和党候选人站台拉票。TIME 政治栏目由此提出一个问题：联邦官员能否这样参与党派政治活动？法律专家和倡导团体认为，这些官员的做法违反了一项实施已有数十年的法律，文章围绕这一争议展开。

paragraphs.en: Legal experts and advocacy groups contend that in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms, members of the Administration have violated a decades-old law.
paragraphs.zh: 法律专家和倡导团体主张，政府成员为了在中期选举前提振共和党人的选情而四处活动，这种做法已经违反了一项已施行数十年的法律。

vocab.meaning_zh: （在争论中）主张、坚称、认为。这是外刊报道争议时的高频词：它只客观转述某方的立场，并不代表编辑部认同，语气比 say 更“有立场之争”。
vocab.example_en: Critics contend that the new rules will mainly hurt small businesses.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者主张，新规主要会伤害小企业。

vocab.meaning_zh: 倡导团体、游说团体；为某一公共议题奔走呼吁的非营利组织，常作为新闻报道中的“第三方声音”出现。
vocab.example_en: Several advocacy groups filed a complaint with the agency last month.
vocab.example_zh: 上个月，几家倡导团体向该机构递交了投诉。

vocab.meaning_zh: 试图、谋求做某事。书面语色彩强，新闻中常用来替代 try to，显得正式而中性。
vocab.example_en: The White House is seeking to calm nervous markets.
vocab.example_zh: 白宫正试图安抚紧张的市场情绪。

vocab.meaning_zh: 提振、拉抬（选情、士气、销量等）；此处指为共和党候选人助选造势。
vocab.example_en: The rally was meant to boost turnout among young voters.
vocab.example_zh: 这场集会的目的是拉高年轻选民的投票率。

vocab.meaning_zh: （美国）中期选举。midterm elections 的口语简称，指两次总统大选之间举行的国会及州级选举，是美国政治的固定说法。
vocab.example_en: Historically, the president's party loses seats in the midterms.
vocab.example_zh: 从历史上看，总统所属的政党往往会在中期选举中丢失席位。

vocab.meaning_zh: （首字母大写的）政府、执政当局；特指现任总统领导下的整个行政班子，而非泛指的“管理”。这是美国政治报道中的固定用法。
vocab.example_en: Officials in the Administration declined to comment.
vocab.example_zh: 该政府内部的官员拒绝置评。

vocab.meaning_zh: 已有数十年历史的、实行了几十年的。新闻中常用来强调某制度“存在已久”，暗含“本应众所周知、不该被忽视”的意味。
vocab.example_en: They are challenging a decades-old precedent.
vocab.example_zh: 他们对一项沿用数十年的判例提出了挑战。

sentences.en: Legal experts and advocacy groups contend that in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms, members of the Administration have violated a decades-old law.
sentences.structure: 主干：Legal experts and advocacy groups（主语）+ contend（谓语）+ that 引导的宾语从句。从句内部：members of the Administration（主语）+ have violated（谓语）+ a decades-old law（宾语）；句首的 in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms 是介词短语作时间/情境状语，其中 ahead of the midterms 又修饰 boost。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句话只有一句，却把“谁在指控谁、凭什么指控”全交代了，值得拆开看。第一，谓语用 contend 而非 say 或 claim，表明这只是原告一方的“主张”，判决未定，媒体因此保持中立。第二，真正的“违法行为”落在宾语从句的 have violated a decades-old law，现在完成时强调“已经发生且后果延续”。第三，介词短语 in seeking to... 被提到从句主语之前，是为了先交代“助选”这个背景，再点出“违法”这一落点，避免句子头重脚轻，也让读者的注意力停在句末的 a decades-old law 上，这恰好是下文要追问的争议焦点。翻译时中文习惯先说背景，所以“为了……而四处活动，这种做法已经违反了……”的顺序反而更自然。

background.title: 中期选举（midterms）
background.text_zh: 美国中期选举在两次总统大选之间的偶数年 11 月举行，改选全部 435 个众议院席位、约三分之一的参议院席位，以及大量州长和州议席。由于投票率通常低于总统大选，且结果往往被解读为选民对在任总统的“期中打分”，执政党常在中期选举中丢席位。也正因如此，白宫与内阁官员在选前高调助选，历来是敏感话题。

background.title: 这项“数十年历史的法律”通常指《哈奇法》（Hatch Act）
background.text_zh: 1939 年通过的《哈奇法》限制联邦行政部门雇员利用职务之便参与党派政治活动，禁止其在公务时间、公务场所或以官方身份为候选人助选、募款。总统与副总统不受该法部分条款约束，这也正是争议的由来：政府高层到底算“以个人身份参政”，还是“借职务之便助选”？该法由独立的特别检察官办公室（Office of Special Counsel）负责调查与执行，违规者可能面临停职、降职乃至解雇。需要说明的是，上述制度背景用于帮助理解摘要中 decades-old law 的所指，摘要本身并未点名具体法律。

title_en: Why Doctors Are Last to Know What’s in the Drug Supply
excerpt_en: The FDA should create an expedited pathway for clinical tests targeting emerging drug threats, write Dr. Shravani Durbhakula and Jeremy Kourvelas.

enrich.title_zh: 为什么医生总是最后才知道药品供应链里有什么
enrich.summary_zh: 这篇 TIME「Ideas」栏目的文章由 Shravani Durbhakula 医生与 Jeremy Kourvelas 撰写，核心主张是：面对不断涌现的新型药物威胁，美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）应当为针对这类威胁的临床试验开辟一条加速审批通道，让医生能更快掌握药品供应链中到底流通着什么。摘要把要解决的问题和提出的制度性建议浓缩成一句，全文的论证细节未在提要中给出。

paragraphs.en: The FDA should create an expedited pathway for clinical tests targeting emerging drug threats, write Dr. Shravani Durbhakula and Jeremy Kourvelas.
paragraphs.zh: Shravani Durbhakula 医生与 Jeremy Kourvelas 撰文指出，FDA 应当为针对新出现的药物威胁所开展的临床试验，设立一条快速审批通道。

vocab.meaning_zh: 加快的、加急的；指审批、流程被压缩时限、优先处理
vocab.example_en: The agency introduced an expedited review process for rare-disease drugs.
vocab.example_zh: 该机构为罕见病药物引入了加快审评流程。

vocab.meaning_zh: （制度性的）通道、途径；在监管语境中常指正式的审批或准入程序
vocab.example_en: The new law opens a regulatory pathway for over-the-counter hearing aids.
vocab.example_zh: 新法律为非处方助听器开辟了一条监管通道。

vocab.meaning_zh: 临床试验、临床检测；此处指在人体上验证药物或检测手段的研究
vocab.example_en: The vaccine moved into clinical tests after promising animal data.
vocab.example_zh: 在动物实验数据令人鼓舞之后，该疫苗进入了临床试验阶段。

vocab.meaning_zh: 针对、以……为目标对象（动词用法，外刊高频）
vocab.example_en: The program targets teenagers who have never voted.
vocab.example_zh: 该项目针对的是从未投过票的青少年。

vocab.meaning_zh: 新出现的、正在浮现的（多指尚在成形、尚未被充分认识的风险或趋势）
vocab.example_en: Public health officials are tracking an emerging strain of the virus.
vocab.example_zh: 公共卫生官员正在追踪一种新出现的病毒毒株。

vocab.meaning_zh: 药品供应（链）、药物供给；标题中特指市面上流通的药品来源与成分
vocab.example_en: Contamination in the drug supply is hard to detect without testing.
vocab.example_zh: 若不进行检测，药品供应链中的污染很难被发现。

sentences.en: The FDA should create an expedited pathway for clinical tests targeting emerging drug threats, write Dr. Shravani Durbhakula and Jeremy Kourvelas.
sentences.structure: 主干：The FDA should create an expedited pathway（主语 + 情态动词 + 谓语 + 宾语）。修饰：for clinical tests 作 pathway 的后置定语，说明通道是给谁用的；targeting emerging drug threats 是现在分词短语作 clinical tests 的后置定语，说明这些试验针对什么。句末 write... 为报道性倒装式引述结构，主语后置。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句是典型的「观点句 + 归属标记」写法：编辑把作者的核心主张前置，把 write sb. 放在句末，让论点占据句首的注意力位置，同时表明下面的判断属于作者而非本刊。翻译时中文习惯把「某某撰文指出」提前，因为中文的引述标记放在句末会显得突兀。注意 expedited pathway 是监管术语，不是泛指「更快的方法」；clinical tests 前的 for 表示用途，与 targeting 引起的定语层层嵌套，阅读时要先剥离修饰、抓住「FDA 应当设立通道」这一骨架。

background.title: FDA 与「加速通道」这套制度语言
background.text_zh: FDA（美国食品药品监督管理局）负责审批药品与医疗器械上市。在应对紧急或重大公共卫生需求时，它有一套成熟但有限定条件的「加速」工具，例如优先审评（priority review）、突破性疗法认定（breakthrough therapy designation）、加速批准（accelerated approval）以及紧急使用授权（EUA）。这些机制的共同逻辑是：在证据标准上做出部分让步或调整流程时限，以换取更快的可及性，同时附带上市后继续验证的义务。因此「expedited pathway」在英文语境里意味着要修订规则、设立正式程序，而非仅仅「提高效率」。

background.title: 「医生最后才知道」指向的信息不对称
background.text_zh: 标题中的 drug supply 指市面流通的药品本身，而非抽象的「供应」概念。在美国，处方药经由制造商、批发商、药房与药品福利管理公司（PBM）等多层主体流转，临床医生通常只看到最终的药品名称与标签，难以获知成分来源、生产场地或掺假情况。近年芬太尼等强效物质掺入非法药物、以及部分海外生产设施的质量问题，使「供应链透明度」成为公共卫生议题。摘要主张从「临床检测」这一端入手加快研究，正是针对这种医生在信息上处于末端的处境。

title_en: Tony Sharps obituary
excerpt_en: Other lives: Manager of community farms who enjoyed helping people get closer to nature
body_en: My friend Tony Sharps, who has died of cancer aged 72, was a practical and sociable man – he excelled at helping troubled youngsters on the community farms that he managed.

Born in London to Pat (nee Dooley) and Bernard Sharps, whose work as a sales rep for Aer Lingus took the family to Somerset, Tony grew up in the village of Congresbury, although his warm wit and storytelling ability hinted at his Irish heritage. On leaving Backwell school he joined the Merchant Navy aged 16 and spent several years at sea or travelling and working abroad.

Tony found employment in the field of residential childcare before obtaining a community and youth work qualification at Matlock College, Derbyshire. In 1981 he joined Windmill Hill City Farm, Bristol, where he was a youth supervisor and farm manager.

His placement at Windmill Hill sparked his interest in the city farms movement, which aimed to connect people in urban centres with the natural world and to reshape the way children engage with food, nature and sustainability. He was in London for the launch in 1980 of the Federation of City Farms (now part of Social Farms & Gardens), with which he continued to be associated for many years. It has now expanded beyond city farms to encompass a network of community-managed green spaces.

I met him while were both doing VSO in India in the mid-1990s. Tony was proud of his time in the country, where he also ran a farm. He was totally comfortable at home or abroad, quick to befriend strangers, happy to laugh at misunderstandings and himself.

He joined the Lambourne End Centre in Essex as farm coordinator in 2002 and helped establish its reputation for the development of young people. Their motto “Inspired to Inspire” sums him up perfectly. In 2017 Tony was awarded a LEEF (London Environmental Educators’ Forum) fellowship recognising his excellence in environmental and sustainability education. He retired to Wells in 2022.

Despite not having excelled at school, Tony was well-read, thoughtful and intelligent. His ability to create communities and friendships was testament to his warmth and good humour, which he retained during his final treatment in hospital.
Tony is survived by his brothers, Chris and Nick, and his sister, Tess.

enrich.title_zh: 托尼·夏普斯讣告
enrich.summary_zh: 这是一篇朋友撰写的讣告，纪念因癌症去世、享年72岁的托尼·夏普斯。他少年时加入商船队，后来投身寄宿儿童照护与社区青年工作，长期在布里斯托尔的风车山城市农场和埃塞克斯的兰伯恩恩德中心负责农场与青年项目，帮助处境困难的年轻人，曾获伦敦环境教育者论坛研究员称号。

paragraphs.en: My friend Tony Sharps, who has died of cancer aged 72, was a practical and sociable man – he excelled at helping troubled youngsters on the community farms that he managed.
paragraphs.zh: 我的友人托尼·夏普斯因癌症去世，享年72岁。他是个务实且善于交际的人，尤其擅长在自己管理的社区农场上帮助那些处境艰难的青少年。

paragraphs.en: Born in London to Pat (nee Dooley) and Bernard Sharps, whose work as a sales rep for Aer Lingus took the family to Somerset, Tony grew up in the village of Congresbury, although his warm wit and storytelling ability hinted at his Irish heritage. On leaving Backwell school he joined the Merchant Navy aged 16 and spent several years at sea or travelling and working abroad.
paragraphs.zh: 托尼出生于伦敦，母亲是帕特（娘家姓杜利），父亲是伯纳德·夏普斯；父亲在爱尔兰航空做销售代表，这份工作把全家带到了萨默塞特，托尼于是在康斯伯里村长大，不过他的幽默风趣和讲故事的能耐都透着他爱尔兰血统的影子。从巴克韦尔学校毕业后，他16岁加入商船队，此后几年不是在海上，就是在国外旅行和工作。

paragraphs.en: Tony found employment in the field of residential childcare before obtaining a community and youth work qualification at Matlock College, Derbyshire. In 1981 he joined Windmill Hill City Farm, Bristol, where he was a youth supervisor and farm manager.
paragraphs.zh: 托尼先是在寄宿儿童照护领域找到工作，后来在德比郡的马特洛克学院取得了社区与青年工作资格。1981年，他加入布里斯托尔的风车山城市农场，担任青年督导和农场经理。

paragraphs.en: His placement at Windmill Hill sparked his interest in the city farms movement, which aimed to connect people in urban centres with the natural world and to reshape the way children engage with food, nature and sustainability. He was in London for the launch in 1980 of the Federation of City Farms (now part of Social Farms & Gardens), with which he continued to be associated for many years. It has now expanded beyond city farms to encompass a network of community-managed green spaces.
paragraphs.zh: 在风车山的任职激发了他对“城市农场运动”的兴趣，这一运动旨在让都市中心的人们与自然世界建立联系，并重塑孩子们接触食物、自然和可持续理念的方式。1980年城市农场联合会（现为“社会农场与花园”的一部分）成立时，他正在伦敦，此后多年一直与该组织保持联系。该组织如今已不止于城市农场，还涵盖了社区管理的各类绿色空间网络。

paragraphs.en: I met him while were both doing VSO in India in the mid-1990s. Tony was proud of his time in the country, where he also ran a farm. He was totally comfortable at home or abroad, quick to befriend strangers, happy to laugh at misunderstandings and himself.
paragraphs.zh: 我和他相识于上世纪90年代中期，当时我们都在印度参加VSO（海外志愿服务组织）的项目。托尼为自己在印度的那段经历感到自豪，他在那里也经营过一座农场。无论在国内还是国外，他都自在从容，很容易与陌生人交上朋友，也乐于拿误会和自己开玩笑。

paragraphs.en: He joined the Lambourne End Centre in Essex as farm coordinator in 2002 and helped establish its reputation for the development of young people. Their motto “Inspired to Inspire” sums him up perfectly. In 2017 Tony was awarded a LEEF (London Environmental Educators’ Forum) fellowship recognising his excellence in environmental and sustainability education. He retired to Wells in 2022.
paragraphs.zh: 2002年，他以农场协调员的身份加入埃塞克斯的兰伯恩恩德中心，帮助该中心树立起以培养青少年见长的声誉。中心那句“被激励，去激励他人”的格言，恰好可以概括他这个人。2017年，托尼获得伦敦环境教育者论坛（LEEF）的研究员称号，以表彰他在环境与可持续发展教育方面的卓越表现。他于2022年退休，移居韦尔斯。

paragraphs.en: Despite not having excelled at school, Tony was well-read, thoughtful and intelligent. His ability to create communities and friendships was testament to his warmth and good humour, which he retained during his final treatment in hospital.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管在学生时代成绩并不出众，托尼却博览群书、善于思考、颇具智慧。他能营造出一种社群感，也能与人结下友谊，这本身便是他热情善良、幽默可亲的证明；直到在医院接受最后的治疗时，他仍保有这份风趣。

paragraphs.en: Tony is survived by his brothers, Chris and Nick, and his sister, Tess.
paragraphs.zh: 托尼身后留下他的兄弟克里斯和尼克，以及妹妹泰丝。

vocab.meaning_zh: 讣告；逝者生平报道
vocab.example_en: The newspaper published a short obituary of the local teacher.
vocab.example_zh: 报纸刊登了一篇关于这位当地教师的简短讣告。

vocab.meaning_zh: 擅长，在某方面表现突出
vocab.example_en: She has always excelled at working with difficult teenagers.
vocab.example_zh: 她一向擅长与难管的青少年打交道。

vocab.meaning_zh: （女子）娘家姓……的，用于姓氏前
vocab.example_en: She is Mary Smith, nee Jones.
vocab.example_zh: 她是玛丽·史密斯，娘家姓琼斯。

vocab.meaning_zh: 销售代表，推销员（representative 的缩略）
vocab.example_en: He worked as a sales rep for a pharmaceutical company.
vocab.example_zh: 他曾在一家制药公司做销售代表。

vocab.meaning_zh: 暗示，透露出（某种特征或出身）
vocab.example_en: Her accent hints at a childhood spent abroad.
vocab.example_zh: 她的口音透露出童年的海外经历。

vocab.meaning_zh: 寄宿式儿童照护，即照护机构内集中居住的儿童教养工作
vocab.example_en: She has spent ten years in residential childcare.
vocab.example_zh: 她在寄宿式儿童照护领域工作了十年。

vocab.meaning_zh: 引发，激起（兴趣、争论等）
vocab.example_en: The trip sparked her lifelong interest in marine biology.
vocab.example_zh: 那次旅行激起了她对海洋生物学的终身兴趣。

vocab.meaning_zh: 涵盖，包括（范围更广）
vocab.example_en: The network now encompasses over 200 community gardens.
vocab.example_zh: 该网络如今涵盖了200多个社区花园。

vocab.meaning_zh: ……的证明，体现
vocab.example_en: The turnout was a testament to her popularity.
vocab.example_zh: 到场人数之多正是她广受欢迎的证明。

vocab.meaning_zh: 与……交朋友，主动结识
vocab.example_en: He had a knack for befriending strangers within minutes.
vocab.example_zh: 他有本事在几分钟内和陌生人交上朋友。

sentences.en: Born in London to Pat (nee Dooley) and Bernard Sharps, whose work as a sales rep for Aer Lingus took the family to Somerset, Tony grew up in the village of Congresbury, although his warm wit and storytelling ability hinted at his Irish heritage.
sentences.structure: 主干：Tony grew up in the village of Congresbury。修饰：句首 Born in London... 为过去分词短语作状语，说明出生与父母；其中 whose work... 是定语从句修饰 Bernard Sharps；句末 although 引导让步状语从句，与主干构成对比。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句把身世信息大量压进句首的分词状语：先说“生在哪里、父母是谁”，再用非限定定语从句补充父亲的职业如何把家搬到萨默塞特，然后才落到主干“在康斯伯里村长大”。最后的 although 从句在语义上并非单纯转折，而是“虽然说不上显眼，但言谈举止透着爱尔兰气质”，为下文写他的口才与亲和力埋下伏笔。翻译时不宜照搬英语语序，可拆成两三个中文短句。

sentences.en: His placement at Windmill Hill sparked his interest in the city farms movement, which aimed to connect people in urban centres with the natural world and to reshape the way children engage with food, nature and sustainability.
sentences.structure: 主干：His placement ... sparked his interest。修饰：in the city farms movement 是 interest 的后置定语；which 引导非限定定语从句修饰 movement，从句内两个不定式 to connect ... and to reshape ... 由 aimed to 并列带出。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是典型的“主句 + which 释义”结构：前半句交代事件，后半句用定语从句给运动下定义。注意 the way children engage with... 中省略了关系词 that/in which，way 后直接跟从句是外刊常见写法，意为“孩子接触……的方式”。两个不定式并列，分别说明该运动的两大目标——把都市人重新连接到自然，以及改变孩子与食物、自然、可持续理念的关系。

sentences.en: His ability to create communities and friendships was testament to his warmth and good humour, which he retained during his final treatment in hospital.
sentences.structure: 主干：His ability ... was testament to his warmth and good humour。修饰：to create communities and friendships 为不定式作 ability 的后置定语；which 引导非限定定语从句，先行词是 warmth and good humour。
sentences.analysis_zh: 主语 ability 带一个较长的不定式定语，若直译成“他创造社群和友谊的能力”略显生硬，中文可转为“他能营造社群、结下友谊”这样的动词表达。表语 testament to 是讣告、评论中的高频词，意为“证明了……”。句末 which 从句把话题从评价转到临终境况，让结尾带出一种克制的伤感，翻译时宜用分号或“直到……仍……”来承接。

background.title: 城市农场运动与城市农场联合会
background.text_zh: 城市农场（city farm）是20世纪70年代起在英国兴起的社区项目：在城区或近郊开辟小型农场，饲养动物、种植蔬果，向学校、家庭和社区开放，兼具自然教育、志愿服务和青少年帮扶功能。1970年代末，这类农场开始联合起来争取政策与资金支持，1980年城市农场联合会（Federation of City Farms）成立，后来发展为今天的“社会农场与花园”（Social Farms & Gardens），业务也从城市农场扩展到社区花园、社区管理的绿地等。文中提到托尼长期与该组织保持联系，正说明他是这一运动中较早期的参与者。

background.title: VSO 与“商船队”
background.text_zh: VSO 即 Voluntary Service Overseas（海外志愿服务组织），成立于1958年，是英国一家派遣志愿者到发展中国家从事教育、医疗、农业等工作的慈善机构，常被看作英国版的“和平队”，90年代在印度有长期项目；文中“doing VSO in India”即参加该项目做志愿者。Merchant Navy（商船队）不是海军，而是指一国从事商业运输的民用船队；英国商船队历史上接收大量十六七岁的少年做见习水手，因此“16岁加入商船队”在当时并非罕见经历。

title_en: Instagram addicts and alcoholics have something in common | Letter
excerpt_en: Letter: As with alcohol, it is important to establish and follow certain rules when using social media, says John Kirkwood
body_en: Reading the letters about Instagram ( We are reclaiming real life after getting rid of Instagram, 23 October) was like attending the internet equivalent of an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting. The problem in both cases appears to be the user, not the substance – be it booze or social media.

As with alcohol, it is important to establish and follow certain rules. I never post images of my family. I almost never include an image of myself, only if I appear, for example in a group of cyclists. I immediately block any request about which I am suspicious (very easy to spot). And I limit myself to 15 minutes of scrolling through other images.

The cycling account that I run on Instagram – @ncn_sheffield – is a useful way of promoting the activities of Walk Wheel Cycle Trust volunteers and, in return, provides useful links to similar groups. Occasionally, beyond cycling, I have discovered some wonderful stuff. As a brickwork nerd, for instance, @les_briques provides an amazing array of fascinating buildings, some of which I hope to visit and in so doing mix with other humans. John Kirkwood Sheffield
• Have an opinion on anything you’ve read in the Guardian today? Please email us your letter and it will be considered for publication in our letters section.

enrich.title_zh: 玩Instagram上瘾的人和酗酒者有一个共同点｜读者来信
enrich.summary_zh: 一位谢菲尔德读者来信回应《卫报》关于“戒掉Instagram、重拾真实生活”的报道，认为社交媒体上瘾与酗酒相似，问题出在用户身上而非平台本身。他分享了自己的使用规则：不发家人照片、极少露脸、立即拉黑可疑请求、每天浏览不超过15分钟；并说明自己运营的骑行账号如何带来社群联结与现实中的收获。

paragraphs.en: Reading the letters about Instagram ( We are reclaiming real life after getting rid of Instagram, 23 October) was like attending the internet equivalent of an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting. The problem in both cases appears to be the user, not the substance – be it booze or social media.
paragraphs.zh: 读那些关于Instagram的来信（《我们摆脱Instagram之后，正在重拾真实生活》，10月23日），感觉就像参加了一场网络版的匿名戒酒会。这两种情况下，问题似乎都出在“使用者”身上，而不是“东西”本身——不管是酒还是社交媒体。

paragraphs.en: As with alcohol, it is important to establish and follow certain rules. I never post images of my family. I almost never include an image of myself, only if I appear, for example in a group of cyclists. I immediately block any request about which I am suspicious (very easy to spot). And I limit myself to 15 minutes of scrolling through other images.
paragraphs.zh: 和对待酒精一样，重要的是定下规矩并照做。我从不发布家人的照片。我也几乎从不放自己的照片，除非我确实出现在画面里，比如在一群骑行者当中。任何让我起疑的好友请求我都会立刻拉黑（这种请求很好辨认）。另外，我给自己限定：刷别人的图片不超过15分钟。

paragraphs.en: The cycling account that I run on Instagram – @ncn_sheffield – is a useful way of promoting the activities of Walk Wheel Cycle Trust volunteers and, in return, provides useful links to similar groups. Occasionally, beyond cycling, I have discovered some wonderful stuff. As a brickwork nerd, for instance, @les_briques provides an amazing array of fascinating buildings, some of which I hope to visit and in so doing mix with other humans. John Kirkwood Sheffield
paragraphs.zh: 我在Instagram上运营的骑行账号——@ncn_sheffield——是宣传Walk Wheel Cycle Trust志愿者活动的一个有用渠道，反过来也为我提供了通往类似团体的有用链接。偶尔，在骑行之外，我还会发现一些非常精彩的东西。比如，作为一个砖砌建筑迷，@les_briques 发布了大量迷人的建筑图片，其中一些我希望亲自去看看，并在这样做的时候和真实的人打交道。John Kirkwood，谢菲尔德

paragraphs.en: • Have an opinion on anything you’ve read in the Guardian today? Please email us your letter and it will be considered for publication in our letters section.
paragraphs.zh: • 对今天在《卫报》上读到的任何内容有看法吗？请把您的来信发给我们，我们会考虑将其刊登在读者来信版块。

vocab.meaning_zh: 对应物、等同之物（the internet equivalent of an AA meeting 即“网络版的匿名戒酒会”）
vocab.example_en: The virtual conference was the online equivalent of a packed lecture hall.
vocab.example_zh: 这场虚拟会议相当于座无虚席的报告厅的网络版。

vocab.meaning_zh: （此处）成瘾性物质、被依赖的“东西”；此处与“使用者 user”对举，指酒或社交媒体本身
vocab.example_en: Addiction counsellors insist the substance is not the whole story.
vocab.example_zh: 戒瘾咨询师坚持认为，成瘾物质并非事情的全部。

vocab.meaning_zh: 酒（口语，略带贬义或随意色彩）
vocab.example_en: He gave up the booze for a year and felt much better.
vocab.example_zh: 他戒酒一年，感觉好多了。

vocab.meaning_zh: 确立、定下（规则、制度等）
vocab.example_en: It is worth establishing a few ground rules before you start.
vocab.example_zh: 开始之前，先定几条基本规则是值得的。

vocab.meaning_zh: 可疑的；让人起疑的
vocab.example_en: She is suspicious of any message asking for personal details.
vocab.example_zh: 她对任何索要个人信息的消息都心存怀疑。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）认出、辨认出、发现
vocab.example_en: These fake accounts are usually easy to spot.
vocab.example_zh: 这类假账号通常很容易辨认。

vocab.meaning_zh: （在手机上）不断滑动浏览
vocab.example_en: I try not to scroll through the feed right before bed.
vocab.example_zh: 我尽量不在睡前刷信息流。

vocab.meaning_zh: （对某事物）痴迷的人、……迷（brickwork nerd 砖砌建筑迷），此处带自嘲式幽默
vocab.example_en: He is a train nerd who can name every station on the line.
vocab.example_zh: 他是个火车迷，能说出这条线路上每一站的站名。

vocab.meaning_zh: 一大批、一系列（an array of 大量种类繁多的）
vocab.example_en: The site offers an array of photographs from the 1930s.
vocab.example_zh: 这个网站提供了一大批20世纪30年代的照片。

vocab.meaning_zh: 在这样做的时候、借此（正式书面语，回指前面刚提到的动作）
vocab.example_en: She volunteers at the shelter and, in so doing, has made close friends.
vocab.example_zh: 她在收容所做志愿者，并因此结交了亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: Reading the letters about Instagram (We are reclaiming real life after getting rid of Instagram, 23 October) was like attending the internet equivalent of an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting.
sentences.structure: 主干：Reading the letters … was like attending the internet equivalent of an AA meeting（动名词短语作主语 + 系动词 was + 表语 like attending…）／修饰：about Instagram 作后置定语限定 letters；括号内是报名与日期，属出处标注
sentences.analysis_zh: 全句骨架是“读这些信＝参加一场会”，比较结构 be like 把读者体验直接类比。主语用动名词 Reading 而不是“I read”，让语气显得克制、就事论事；把报道标题塞进括号，是英国报纸读者来信栏的常见做法——既交代回应对象，又不打断句子。写作上值得学的是“A 是 B 的网络版”这种类比框架，用一句就把陌生现象挂到读者熟悉的经验上。

sentences.en: The problem in both cases appears to be the user, not the substance – be it booze or social media.
sentences.structure: 主干：The problem appears to be the user（主语 + 系动词 + 不定式表语）／修饰：in both cases 作状语限定 problem；not the substance 与 the user 构成对比；破折号后 be it booze or social media 是让步状语从句，相当于 whether it is booze or social media
sentences.analysis_zh: appears to be 是典型的“留有余地”的评论口吻，比 is 更谨慎。not the substance 用否定补语把对比钉死：责任在“人”不在“物”。破折号后的 be it A or B 是外刊高频的虚拟让步结构（省略了 whether），作用是把抽象名词 substance 落到具体例子上，避免读者不知所指。

sentences.en: The cycling account that I run on Instagram – @ncn_sheffield – is a useful way of promoting the activities of Walk Wheel Cycle Trust volunteers and, in return, provides useful links to similar groups.
sentences.structure: 主干：The cycling account is a useful way … and provides useful links …（一个主语带两个并列谓语 is 和 provides）／修饰：that I run on Instagram 是定语从句修饰 account；破折号中间的 @ncn_sheffield 是插入的同位成分；of promoting… 是 way 的后置定语；in return 作插入状语
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子较长，但主干只有“账号是途径、并提供链接”两件事，先抓住这个再挂修饰就不会乱。定语从句用 run 这个动词（run an account＝运营账号）而不是 I have，暗示投入与责任。and 后面再起一个谓语 provides，使句子从“我宣传别人”转到“别人也帮到我”，这正是该段要表达的互惠关系；in return 是标志性提示词。

background.title: 匿名戒酒会（Alcoholics Anonymous）与“戒断叙事”
background.text_zh: Alcoholics Anonymous 是1930年代起源于美国的戒酒互助组织，成员以“我是酒鬼”自报身份，通过定期聚会分享经历、互相监督，配合著名的“十二步法”戒酒。其聚会的基本形态就是围坐一圈、轮流讲述自己如何被某种东西控制又如何抵抗。来信者说读那些“戒Instagram”的信像参加网络版AA会议，正是抓住这种“集体忏悔＋互相打气”的形式相似性；这也解释了为什么他把上瘾对象称为 the substance（成瘾物质），并把它扩展到社交媒体。

background.title: 《卫报》读者来信版与“| Letter”标记
background.text_zh: 英国《卫报》每天设有 Letters 版（除周日外），刊登读者对近期报道的简短回应，文末署“姓名＋所在城市”，如本文的 John Kirkwood, Sheffield。标题由编辑部拟定，常用冒号或竖线引出核心判断；此文标题后面的“| Letter”是网站给体裁打的标签，说明它不是记者报道，而是一封读者来信。第4段的征稿启事是该栏目固定的尾巴，几乎每篇末尾都会出现，因此不必当作文章正文来读。来信中提到的 @ncn_sheffield 从命名看与英国国家骑行网络（National Cycle Network，由慈善机构 Sustrans 维护）在谢菲尔德的地方账号有关，但作者本人只说明这是他在运营的骑行账号。

title_en: Tusk defends overhaul of Poland’s constitutional court despite protests
excerpt_en: Prime minister says shake-up is vital to restore tribunal crippled by years of political disputes
body_en: Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has vowed to see through a contested overhaul of the country’s constitutional court, declaring that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise”.

In a prime-time television address on Saturday night, Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes.
Related: Riot police deployed to Poland’s constitutional court after judge suspended
Paralysed for more than a decade, the court sat at the core of rule of law clashes between the rightwing Law and Justice (PiS) party and the EU during the party’s eight-year rule.

Since returning to office in 2023, the centre-right Tusk has sought to unwind those judicial changes, but his agenda has been frustrated by opposition-aligned presidents with extensive veto powers. Earlier this year, president Karol Nawrocki refused to swear in five judges approved by parliament.

The crisis flared again on Friday when a group of government-backed judges attempted to seize procedural control of the tribunal, suspending the PiS-appointed chief judge and deputy and prompting street protests.
Defending the action, Tusk said “there was never any doubt that the court in the form imposed by PiS was not a genuine court”, citing adverse rulings from European tribunals.
He compared the opposition outrage to “a thief snatching an elderly woman’s handbag, running off, and when he is caught, he screams that he is subjected to violence”.

Tusk said: “Let’s call things for what they are: for years, there have been organisations and politicians in Poland who seek to destroy democracy and the rule of law. It is no coincidence they find support among pro-Russian forces globally.”

He later highlighted that Russia’s former president Dmitry Medvedev had joined the opposition in an outcry over the changes, accusing Warsaw of “a constitutional coup” and “hounding the conservatives”. “And everything is clear,” Tusk said.

He also criticised opposition-aligned Nawrocki for joining the protests on Friday night and forcing his entry into the court’s building to intervene. “In a democratic state, no politician can enter a court to issue orders or intimidate judges – not even the president,” Tusk said. “We Poles have succeeded too well in building a strong state to surrender now.”
He said it was the government’s duty to ensure its security and the conditions necessary for the court to operate. “And I intend to fulfil that duty,” he said.
On Saturday, the European Commission urged Nawrocki to approve the new judges who were nominated by parliament, so the court could function in line with the constitution and EU law.
A spokesperson for the commission said its executive was “following closely” the events in Poland.

“It is for the Polish authorities to ensure that the constitutional tribunal can function in accordance with the Polish constitution and in respect of the relevant case law of the court of justice of the European Union,” the spokesperson said, appearing to ally the bloc with the Polish government.

However, the spokesperson also highlighted that the European court of human rights issued an interim finding in May that obliged Polish authorities to “refrain from hindering the taking up and exercise of judicial duties” by judges who are still waiting to be sworn in.
The confrontation sets the battle lines before next year’s parliamentary election, with polls pointing to a close race between Tusk’s broad coalition and the nationalist right.
However, experts remain divided over whether the government’s procedural gambit at the court is lawful.
Poland’s Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights said on Saturday the legal basis for the temporary suspension was “questionable”, warning it would “not contribute” to restoring the court.

The foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, conceded that the events outside the court were “not elegant”, but insisted: “The alternative was to concede an unconstitutional transformation of Poland into a presidential republic.”

Nawrocki held some cross-party political talks on Saturday, with no apparent breakthrough. His senior aide, Zbigniew Bogucki, responded to Tusk’s address, calling the prime minister “a pathological liar, who is setting Poland ablaze”.

enrich.title_zh: 图斯克为波兰宪法法庭改革辩护，抗议声中坚持推进
enrich.summary_zh: 波兰总理图斯克发表电视讲话，坚持推进对宪法法庭的改组。此前政府支持的法官将PiS任命的首席法官停职，引发街头抗议和防暴警察进驻法院。图斯克称该法庭早已被政治纷争弄得瘫痪、并非真正的法院，并把反对派的指责斥为贼喊捉贼。欧盟委员会敦促总统批准新法官，但也提醒欧洲人权法院的临时裁定；专家对政府此举是否合法仍有分歧。

paragraphs.en: Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has vowed to see through a contested overhaul of the country’s constitutional court, declaring that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise”.
paragraphs.zh: 波兰总理唐纳德·图斯克誓言要将他备受争议的宪法法庭改革推行到底，并宣称“在某些问题上，不存在妥协的余地”。

paragraphs.en: In a prime-time television address on Saturday night, Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes.
paragraphs.zh: 在周六晚间的电视黄金时段讲话中，图斯克态度强硬。前一晚的抗议迫使防暴警察被调来守卫法院大楼，但他仍表示，这场改组对于重振一个被多年政治纷争弄得瘫痪的法庭至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Related: Riot police deployed to Poland’s constitutional court after judge suspended
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：法官被停职后，防暴警察进驻波兰宪法法庭

paragraphs.en: Paralysed for more than a decade, the court sat at the core of rule of law clashes between the rightwing Law and Justice (PiS) party and the EU during the party’s eight-year rule.
paragraphs.zh: 该法庭瘫痪已十余年。在右翼法律与公正党（PiS）执政的八年间，它一直处于该党与欧盟之间法治冲突的核心。

paragraphs.en: Since returning to office in 2023, the centre-right Tusk has sought to unwind those judicial changes, but his agenda has been frustrated by opposition-aligned presidents with extensive veto powers. Earlier this year, president Karol Nawrocki refused to swear in five judges approved by parliament.
paragraphs.zh: 自2023年重新执政以来，中右翼的图斯克一直试图撤销这些司法改动，但他的议程屡屡被与反对派结盟、握有广泛否决权的总统所挫败。今年早些时候，总统卡罗尔·纳夫罗茨基拒绝为议会批准的五名法官主持宣誓就职。

paragraphs.en: The crisis flared again on Friday when a group of government-backed judges attempted to seize procedural control of the tribunal, suspending the PiS-appointed chief judge and deputy and prompting street protests.
paragraphs.zh: 周五，危机再度爆发：一群获得政府支持的法官试图夺取该法庭的程序控制权，将PiS任命的首席法官和副庭长停职，并由此引发街头抗议。

paragraphs.en: Defending the action, Tusk said “there was never any doubt that the court in the form imposed by PiS was not a genuine court”, citing adverse rulings from European tribunals.
paragraphs.zh: 图斯克为该行动辩护，援引欧洲各法庭作出的不利裁决，称“从来没有人怀疑，PiS强加的那种形态的法院并不是一个真正的法院”。

paragraphs.en: He compared the opposition outrage to “a thief snatching an elderly woman’s handbag, running off, and when he is caught, he screams that he is subjected to violence”.
paragraphs.zh: 他把反对派的愤怒比作“一个小偷抢了老妇人的手袋，拔腿就跑，被抓到后却大喊自己遭到了暴力对待”。

paragraphs.en: Tusk said: “Let’s call things for what they are: for years, there have been organisations and politicians in Poland who seek to destroy democracy and the rule of law. It is no coincidence they find support among pro-Russian forces globally.”
paragraphs.zh: 图斯克说：“我们实话实说：多年来，波兰一直有一些组织和政客企图摧毁民主与法治。他们在全球亲俄势力当中获得支持，绝非巧合。”

paragraphs.en: He later highlighted that Russia’s former president Dmitry Medvedev had joined the opposition in an outcry over the changes, accusing Warsaw of “a constitutional coup” and “hounding the conservatives”. “And everything is clear,” Tusk said.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后强调，俄罗斯前总统德米特里·梅德韦杰夫也加入了反对派对这些改革的声讨，指责华沙搞“宪法政变”、“迫害保守派”。“这下一切都清楚了，”图斯克说。
