paragraphs.zh: 市规划委员会本月的投票酝酿了四年，也是对拟建的“乔·路易斯绿道”（Joe Louis Greenway）周边土地进行整体评估的一部分。这条供步行和骑行的绿道将横贯全城，目前已在施工中。

vocab.meaning_zh: 重新划分用地性质，重新区划（改变某地块允许的用途）
vocab.example_en: The rezoning would bar concrete plants from the neighborhood.
vocab.example_zh: 重新区划将禁止混凝土搅拌站进入该社区。

vocab.meaning_zh: （行动的）自由空间，自主余地（熟词僻义，非“纬度”）
vocab.example_en: Regulators gave the company considerable latitude in fixing the violations.
vocab.example_zh: 监管机构在整改违规问题上给了这家公司相当大的自由空间。

vocab.meaning_zh: （一块）地块，地皮
vocab.example_en: Crown bought dozens of parcels on the block.
vocab.example_zh: Crown 在该街区买下了数十块地。

vocab.meaning_zh: 缓冲地带，隔离带
vocab.example_en: The planners wanted a buffer between homes and the plant.
vocab.example_zh: 规划人员希望在住宅与工厂之间留出缓冲地带。

vocab.meaning_zh: 光秃秃的，空置无建筑的
vocab.example_en: Most of the company's lots in the area remain barren.
vocab.example_zh: 该公司在该区域的大多数地块仍是空地。

vocab.meaning_zh: 立足点，落脚点，初步的控制
vocab.example_en: The family gained a foothold in the neighborhood decades ago.
vocab.example_zh: 这个家族几十年前就在该社区站稳了脚跟。

vocab.meaning_zh: 改变立场，食言，打退堂鼓
vocab.example_en: The city would be backtracking on its promise to the developer.
vocab.example_zh: 市政府将等于背弃对开发商的承诺。

vocab.meaning_zh: 使贬值，降低价值
vocab.example_en: The lawyers argued that the rezoning would devalue the property.
vocab.example_zh: 律师们主张，重新区划会令该地产贬值。

vocab.meaning_zh: 史无前例的，首个此类别的
vocab.example_en: The city signed a first-of-its-kind enforcement agreement with the company.
vocab.example_zh: 该市与这家公司签署了一份史无前例的执法协议。

vocab.meaning_zh: 土地置换，换地交易
vocab.example_en: The land swap cleared the way for a new assembly plant.
vocab.example_zh: 这笔土地置换为新组装厂铺平了道路。

sentences.en: The planning recommendation comes after a BridgeDetroit and ProPublica investigation this year revealed how city officials helped Crown Enterprises, a real estate company owned by Detroit’s wealthy Moroun family, obtain property in Cadillac Heights and then provided latitude when its Kronos facility violated environmental laws.
sentences.structure: 主干：The planning recommendation comes after an investigation（主句） / 修饰：this year 修饰 investigation；revealed 后接 how 引导的宾语从句；a real estate company owned by… 是 Crown Enterprises 的同位语；when its Kronos facility violated environmental laws 是宾语从句内的时间状语从句
sentences.analysis_zh: 主句只有“建议是在调查之后到来”这一层意思，信息重心全落在 after 引导的时间状语里。作者把调查内容塞进一个 how 从句，用“帮助拿地 + 违法时给自由”两个动作并列，一句话交代了整篇报道的核心指控。同位语用过去分词 owned by 后置，既解释了 Crown 是谁，又点明其与莫朗家族的关系，为后文的利益关联埋线。翻译时宜拆成“揭露：……，而……”，保持两个动作的并列张力。

sentences.en: City Council members, acting on a recommendation last week from planning officials, will soon consider a rezoning measure that would restrict industrial activity at the site of the Kronos concrete plant and surrounding area.
sentences.structure: 主干：City Council members will soon consider a rezoning measure / 修饰：acting on a recommendation… 为现在分词短语作状语，说明依据；that would restrict… 为定语从句修饰 measure；at the site of… and surrounding area 为地点状语
sentences.analysis_zh: 主语和谓语被一个较长的分词状语隔开，这是英文新闻句的典型写法：先点明动作的依据，再交代动作本身。定语从句用 would 而非 will，是虚拟/推测语气，因为议案尚未通过，只表示“将会产生的效果”。restrict industrial activity 是全句的关键动词短语，正是“限制扩张”的法律落点。

sentences.en: Attorney Melvin Butch Hollowell also said if the rezoning goes through, the city would be backtracking on its commitment to support Crown’s development in Cadillac Heights.
sentences.structure: 主干：Attorney Melvin Butch Hollowell also said + 宾语从句 / 宾语从句内部：if the rezoning goes through（条件状语从句）+ the city would be backtracking on its commitment / 修饰：to support Crown’s development in Cadillac Heights 为不定式短语修饰 commitment
sentences.analysis_zh: said 后面省略了 that，直接跟宾语从句；从句本身是“条件 + 主句”结构。goes through 用一般现在时表将来，是条件句的常规用法；主句用 would be backtracking 进行时，强调“将处于一种出尔反尔的状态”，比 would backtrack 更有画面感。commitment to 中的 to 是介词，故后接动名词性名词 development，而非不定式。

background.title: 美国的区划（zoning）制度
background.text_zh: 美国城市通过“区划”规定每块地允许的用途与建筑强度，常见分类包括住宅、商业、轻工业、重工业等。用地性质一旦确定，业主只能在其范围内开发；改变性质须经规划委员会建议、市议会表决，并通常要举行公开听证，业主可提出异议甚至诉讼。因此，把某片区从“重工业”改为“轻工业”，实质就是禁止新建混凝土搅拌站这类重污染设施，而仓库等仍可建设。这也是本案双方围绕“重新区划是否等于变相征收、是否使地产贬值”展开法律博弈的原因。

background.title: 莫朗家族、Crown Enterprises 与 Stellantis 工厂
background.text_zh: 莫朗家族（Moroun family）是底特律最知名的地产富豪家族之一，长期拥有连接底特律与加拿大温莎的大使桥（Ambassador Bridge），以强硬维权和大量持有市中心周边地块著称。Crown Enterprises 是其旗下房地产公司。2019 年的土地置换中，Crown 交出城市另一处土地，使 Stellantis（原菲亚特克莱斯勒，旗下有 Jeep 等品牌）得以在该处建设底特律三十年来首座新整车厂，而 Crown 则获得 Cadillac Heights 的多块土地。这一段交易背景解释了市政府为何在道义与法律上都对 Crown 负有“支持再开发”的承诺。

title_en: Top U.S. Health Official Backed a Medication Policy Shift That Benefited a Company She Has Stock In
excerpt_en: The post Top U.S. Health Official Backed a Medication Policy Shift That Benefited a Company She Has Stock In appeared first on ProPublica.
body_en: Alicia Jackson, director of the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, speaks at an event earlier this year. Photo illustration by ProPublica. Photo by Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images. Last November, the Department of Health and Human Services announced the elimination of “black box” warnings on hormone replacement therapies, aiming to reverse nearly two decades of stigma surrounding a key treatment for menopause symptoms.

Among the officials at a press conference about the decision was Alicia Jackson, director of a federal health agency that invests taxpayer money in medical technology and research. As Jackson stood behind a lectern adorned with the HHS logo, she praised the new policy, calling it a victory for women and science.

“Today we have the opportunity to add up to a decade of healthy years to the life of every woman that you love,” Jackson said. “The science is clear: Hormone therapy is safe and effective. And it is hugely beneficial to the vast majority of women.”
Less clear that day were the financial benefits the new policy could bring Jackson, according to disclosure records obtained by ProPublica.

Jackson is the founder and former chief executive of Evernow, an online platform that connects women with medical experts who treat the symptoms of menopause. Although she left for federal service last year, she kept at least $115,000 in Evernow stock and an unknown amount of stock options, records show.

Those are just part of a multimillion-dollar portfolio Jackson holds with her husband, a venture capitalist, that poses potential conflicts of interest with her work overseeing the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, known as ARPA-H.

It’s unclear what role, if any, Jackson played in dropping the black box warning, the most serious type of federal safety warning that is reserved for drugs with severe side effects or life-threatening risks. A different agency, the Food and Drug Administration, regulates drugs, and its panel of experts had recommended an end to the warning requirement months before Jackson arrived in government.

But ethics experts called Jackson’s official endorsement of the warning removal “alarming” and an “obvious conflict of interest,” noting federal law prohibits government employees from participating “personally and substantially” in matters that could influence their personal finances — even making statements at a press conference or in a news release, as she also did.

“We should care because her company is apparently intending to profit off this change in policy that she endorsed as a government official while still retaining a financial interest in the company,” said Virginia Canter, who served as an ethics lawyer at the White House, Treasury Department and Securities and Exchange Commission during the presidencies of George H.W. Bush, Bill Clinton, George W. Bush and Barack Obama.
“I say it puts her within the zone of a potential violation,” she said.
Months after the announced end to the warning notices, Evernow launched a nationwide expansion.

Under federal law, agency officials like Jackson are required to submit financial disclosure forms, which must then be certified as complying with ethics laws. But Jackson’s two financial disclosures — filed last October and two months ago — remain uncertified. Canter said it is not unusual for an agency’s ethics office to ask the inspector general to investigate if staff cannot certify that an individual’s disclosure forms meet ethics standards.

Over two months, ProPublica sought comment from Jackson and submitted questions about her work, investments and ethics records. Jackson did not respond, and HHS never addressed our detailed questions.

But in a statement to ProPublica last week, an agency spokesperson said Jackson has been placed on administrative leave and HHS would “assess the facts before determining any change in her status. HHS requires all officials to comply with federal ethics laws, regulations, and policies.”
HHS declined to answer additional questions about the reasons for Jackson’s leave, the decision’s timing or whether the inspector general was investigating.

Earlier this week, Bloomberg Law reported on the HHS statement that Jackson was on leave and made public a draft memo by one of the agency’s senior officials that would have granted Jackson a conflict waiver involving many of her and her husband’s extensive investments. Since she joined ARPA-H, the memo said, Jackson and her husband’s financial ties required her to recuse herself from “a significant portion” of her duties, including discussions about funding awarded by her agency. The waiver named 30 investments and would have allowed Jackson to take part in decisions that could affect those interests. Evernow is not listed.

Bloomberg reported that two firms with ties to Jackson sought ARPA-H funding, but it was unclear if either received any. HHS did not respond to ProPublica’s questions asking whether the waiver was ever granted or if the firms had received money from ARPA-H. The Office of Government Ethics does not list Jackson among federal officials who have received waivers.

Jackson’s disclosures are among 2,400 added Thursday to ProPublica’s Trump Team Financials database, a searchable tool launched in March. The records detail the finances of more than 2,300 officials appointed by President Donald Trump. Since last year, we’ve requested disclosure records from 127 federal agencies and the White House. Disclosures from roughly 1,500 appointees remain unreleased.

The Trump administration’s massive cuts to the federal bureaucracy have taken a toll on the ranks of ethics staff. By the end of 2025, there were 274 fewer full-time ethics officials, according to a recent analysis of federal survey records by the government watchdog group Campaign Legal Center. Some agencies said the losses hampered ethics officers’ ability to conduct training and monitor employee compliance.

enrich.title_zh: 美国高级卫生官员支持的一项用药政策转变，让她自己持股的公司从中受益
enrich.summary_zh: ProPublica调查发现，美国卫生高级研究计划局（ARPA-H）局长艾丽西亚·杰克逊在HHS宣布取消激素替代疗法“黑框警告”的发布会上公开为该政策背书，而她本人仍是更年期在线诊疗平台Evernow的创始人和大股东，至少持有11.5万美元股票及数量不详的期权。伦理专家认为这构成明显利益冲突、涉嫌违规。杰克逊的两份财产申报至今未获认证，她本人已被安排行政休假，HHS拒绝进一步说明。

paragraphs.en: Alicia Jackson, director of the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, speaks at an event earlier this year. Photo illustration by ProPublica. Photo by Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images. Last November, the Department of Health and Human Services announced the elimination of “black box” warnings on hormone replacement therapies, aiming to reverse nearly two decades of stigma surrounding a key treatment for menopause symptoms.
paragraphs.zh: （图注）美国卫生高级研究计划局局长艾丽西亚·杰克逊今年早些时候在一次活动上发言。图片合成：ProPublica；摄影：Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images。去年11月，美国卫生与公众服务部宣布取消激素替代疗法上的“黑框”警告，意在扭转近二十年来围绕这一更年期症状关键疗法所蒙受的污名。

paragraphs.en: Among the officials at a press conference about the decision was Alicia Jackson, director of a federal health agency that invests taxpayer money in medical technology and research. As Jackson stood behind a lectern adorned with the HHS logo, she praised the new policy, calling it a victory for women and science.
paragraphs.zh: 在这场宣布该决定的新闻发布会上，出席官员中就有艾丽西亚·杰克逊——她领导的联邦卫生机构负责把纳税人的钱投向医疗技术与研究。杰克逊站在印有HHS标志的讲台后，对新政策大加赞赏，称这是女性与科学的胜利。

paragraphs.en: “Today we have the opportunity to add up to a decade of healthy years to the life of every woman that you love,” Jackson said. “The science is clear: Hormone therapy is safe and effective. And it is hugely beneficial to the vast majority of women.”
paragraphs.zh: “今天，我们有机会为你所爱的每一位女性的生命，增添多达十年的健康岁月。”杰克逊说，“科学结论很清楚：激素疗法安全、有效，而且对绝大多数女性大有裨益。”

paragraphs.en: Less clear that day were the financial benefits the new policy could bring Jackson, according to disclosure records obtained by ProPublica.
paragraphs.zh: 但根据ProPublica获取的财产申报记录，当天并不那么清楚的是：这项新政策可能给杰克逊本人带来怎样的经济利益。

paragraphs.en: Jackson is the founder and former chief executive of Evernow, an online platform that connects women with medical experts who treat the symptoms of menopause. Although she left for federal service last year, she kept at least $115,000 in Evernow stock and an unknown amount of stock options, records show.
paragraphs.zh: 杰克逊是Evernow的创始人兼前首席执行官，这是一个把女性与治疗更年期症状的医学专家对接起来的在线平台。记录显示，尽管她去年离职进入联邦政府任职，但仍保留了至少价值11.5万美元的Evernow股票，以及数量不详的股票期权。

paragraphs.en: Those are just part of a multimillion-dollar portfolio Jackson holds with her husband, a venture capitalist, that poses potential conflicts of interest with her work overseeing the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, known as ARPA-H.
paragraphs.zh: 这些只是杰克逊与丈夫（一位风险投资人）共同持有的数百万美元投资组合的一部分，而该组合与她在美国卫生高级研究计划局（简称ARPA-H）的监管工作之间存在潜在利益冲突。

paragraphs.en: It’s unclear what role, if any, Jackson played in dropping the black box warning, the most serious type of federal safety warning that is reserved for drugs with severe side effects or life-threatening risks. A different agency, the Food and Drug Administration, regulates drugs, and its panel of experts had recommended an end to the warning requirement months before Jackson arrived in government.
paragraphs.zh: 目前尚不清楚杰克逊在取消黑框警告一事中究竟起了什么作用（如果有的话）。黑框警告是联邦安全警告中最严重的一类，只用于副作用严重或具有致命风险的药物。监管药物的是另一家机构——美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA），而早在杰克逊进入政府任职数月之前，其专家小组就已建议终止这项警告要求。

paragraphs.en: But ethics experts called Jackson’s official endorsement of the warning removal “alarming” and an “obvious conflict of interest,” noting federal law prohibits government employees from participating “personally and substantially” in matters that could influence their personal finances — even making statements at a press conference or in a news release, as she also did.
paragraphs.zh: 但伦理专家称，杰克逊以官方身份为取消警告背书“令人震惊”，是“明显的利益冲突”，并指出联邦法律禁止政府雇员“亲自且实质性地”参与可能影响其个人财务的事务——甚至包括在新闻发布会上或新闻稿中发表声明，而她也确实这么做了。

paragraphs.en: “We should care because her company is apparently intending to profit off this change in policy that she endorsed as a government official while still retaining a financial interest in the company,” said Virginia Canter, who served as an ethics lawyer at the White House, Treasury Department and Securities and Exchange Commission during the presidencies of George H.W. Bush, Bill Clinton, George W. Bush and Barack Obama.
paragraphs.zh: “我们应当关注这件事，因为她的公司显然打算从这项政策转变中获利，而这项转变正是她以政府官员身份背书的，同时她还保留着对该公司的经济利益。”弗吉尼亚·坎特说。她曾在乔治·H·W·布什、比尔·克林顿、乔治·W·布什和巴拉克·奥巴马四任总统时期，先后在白宫、财政部和证券交易委员会担任伦理律师。

paragraphs.en: “I say it puts her within the zone of a potential violation,” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “我认为这已经把她放进了可能违规的区间里。”她说。

paragraphs.en: Months after the announced end to the warning notices, Evernow launched a nationwide expansion.
paragraphs.zh: 在宣布终止该警告标识数月之后，Evernow启动了全国范围的扩张。

paragraphs.en: Under federal law, agency officials like Jackson are required to submit financial disclosure forms, which must then be certified as complying with ethics laws. But Jackson’s two financial disclosures — filed last October and two months ago — remain uncertified. Canter said it is not unusual for an agency’s ethics office to ask the inspector general to investigate if staff cannot certify that an individual’s disclosure forms meet ethics standards.
paragraphs.zh: 根据联邦法律，像杰克逊这样的机构官员必须提交财产申报表，这些申报表随后须被认证为符合伦理法律。但杰克逊的两份财产申报——分别于去年10月和两个月前提交——至今仍未获认证。坎特说，如果伦理办公室的工作人员无法确认某人的申报表符合伦理标准，由机构伦理办公室请监察长介入调查，这种情况并不罕见。

paragraphs.en: Over two months, ProPublica sought comment from Jackson and submitted questions about her work, investments and ethics records. Jackson did not respond, and HHS never addressed our detailed questions.
paragraphs.zh: 在两个月的时间里，ProPublica多次向杰克逊寻求置评，并就她的工作、投资和伦理记录提交了问题。杰克逊没有回应，HHS也始终没有回答我们的详细提问。

paragraphs.en: But in a statement to ProPublica last week, an agency spokesperson said Jackson has been placed on administrative leave and HHS would “assess the facts before determining any change in her status. HHS requires all officials to comply with federal ethics laws, regulations, and policies.”
paragraphs.zh: 但在上周给ProPublica的一份声明中，该机构的一位发言人称杰克逊已被安排行政休假，HHS将“在评估事实之后再决定是否改变她的身份状态。HHS要求所有官员遵守联邦伦理法律、法规和政策”。

paragraphs.en: HHS declined to answer additional questions about the reasons for Jackson’s leave, the decision’s timing or whether the inspector general was investigating.
paragraphs.zh: 对于杰克逊休假的原因、这一决定的时机，以及监察长是否正在调查等进一步问题，HHS拒绝作答。

paragraphs.en: Earlier this week, Bloomberg Law reported on the HHS statement that Jackson was on leave and made public a draft memo by one of the agency’s senior officials that would have granted Jackson a conflict waiver involving many of her and her husband’s extensive investments. Since she joined ARPA-H, the memo said, Jackson and her husband’s financial ties required her to recuse herself from “a significant portion” of her duties, including discussions about funding awarded by her agency. The waiver named 30 investments and would have allowed Jackson to take part in decisions that could affect those interests. Evernow is not listed.
paragraphs.zh: 本周早些时候，彭博法律（Bloomberg Law）报道了HHS关于杰克逊休假的声明，并公开了该机构一位高级官员起草的一份备忘录草案，该草案原本要给杰克逊一项利益冲突豁免，涉及她和丈夫的众多大额投资。备忘录称，自她加入ARPA-H以来，杰克逊与丈夫的财务关系使她必须回避“相当一部分”职责，包括有关其所在机构拨款事宜的讨论。该豁免列出了30项投资，一旦获批便可允许杰克逊参与可能影响这些利益的决策。Evernow并不在名单上。

paragraphs.en: Bloomberg reported that two firms with ties to Jackson sought ARPA-H funding, but it was unclear if either received any. HHS did not respond to ProPublica’s questions asking whether the waiver was ever granted or if the firms had received money from ARPA-H. The Office of Government Ethics does not list Jackson among federal officials who have received waivers.
paragraphs.zh: 彭博报道称，有两家与杰克逊有关联的公司曾申请ARPA-H的资金，但不清楚其中是否有任何一家拿到钱。对于该豁免是否最终获批、这两家公司是否从ARPA-H获得过资金，HHS没有回应ProPublica的提问。在政府伦理办公室（Office of Government Ethics）公布的获得豁免的联邦官员名单中，也没有杰克逊的名字。

paragraphs.en: Jackson’s disclosures are among 2,400 added Thursday to ProPublica’s Trump Team Financials database, a searchable tool launched in March. The records detail the finances of more than 2,300 officials appointed by President Donald Trump. Since last year, we’ve requested disclosure records from 127 federal agencies and the White House. Disclosures from roughly 1,500 appointees remain unreleased.
paragraphs.zh: 周四，ProPublica的“特朗普团队财务状况”数据库一次性新增了2400份申报记录，杰克逊的申报也在其中。该数据库是今年3月上线的可检索工具，详细记录了唐纳德·特朗普总统任命的两千三百多名官员的财务状况。自去年以来，我们已向127个联邦机构及白宫索取申报记录。目前仍有约1500名被任命者的申报材料没有公开。

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration’s massive cuts to the federal bureaucracy have taken a toll on the ranks of ethics staff. By the end of 2025, there were 274 fewer full-time ethics officials, according to a recent analysis of federal survey records by the government watchdog group Campaign Legal Center. Some agencies said the losses hampered ethics officers’ ability to conduct training and monitor employee compliance.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府对联邦官僚体系的大规模削减，已经损害了伦理工作人员队伍。根据政府监督组织“竞选法律中心”（Campaign Legal Center）最近对联邦调查记录的分析，到2025年底，全职伦理官员减少了274人。一些机构表示，人员流失削弱了伦理官员开展培训、监督员工合规的能力。

vocab.meaning_zh: 黑框警告（美国FDA药品标签上最严厉的安全警示，用粗黑边框圈出，通常用于有严重甚至致命风险的药物）
vocab.example_en: The FDA added a black box warning to the drug after reports of severe liver damage.
vocab.example_zh: 在出现严重肝损伤的报告后，FDA在该药品标签上加注了黑框警告。

vocab.meaning_zh: 污名，羞耻感；（某事物因被误解而背负的）负面标签
vocab.example_en: The campaign aims to remove the stigma surrounding menopause in the workplace.
vocab.example_zh: 这项活动旨在消除职场中对更年期的污名化。

vocab.meaning_zh: 激素替代疗法（HRT），通过补充雌激素等缓解更年期症状的治疗方式
vocab.example_en: Hormone replacement therapy can relieve hot flashes but is not suitable for everyone.
vocab.example_zh: 激素替代疗法可以缓解潮热，但并非人人适用。

vocab.meaning_zh: （供演讲者放讲稿的）斜面讲台、演讲台
vocab.example_en: She stepped behind the lectern and waited for the applause to die down.
vocab.example_zh: 她走到讲台后，等掌声平息下来。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）投资组合，一个人持有的全部金融资产
vocab.example_en: Ethics rules require officials to disclose any holdings in their investment portfolio.
vocab.example_zh: 伦理规则要求官员披露其投资组合中的任何持股。

vocab.meaning_zh: （因利益冲突而）主动回避、退出某项事务
vocab.example_en: The official recused herself from the contract review because her brother owned the bidding firm.
vocab.example_zh: 由于她弟弟拥有投标公司，这位官员回避了该合同的审核。

vocab.meaning_zh: 豁免（书），官方允许某人不受某项规定的约束
vocab.example_en: He was granted a waiver allowing him to work on issues affecting his former employer.
vocab.example_zh: 他获得了一份豁免，可以参与涉及其前雇主的议题。

vocab.meaning_zh: 行政休假（通常带有停职调查性质，当事人仍保留职务和薪水）
vocab.example_en: The director was placed on administrative leave pending an internal investigation.
vocab.example_zh: 在内部调查进行期间，该局长被安排行政休假。

vocab.meaning_zh: 背书，公开支持、认可（尤指有影响力者或官方人士的公开表态）
vocab.example_en: Her endorsement of the policy gave it credibility with the public.
vocab.example_zh: 她对这项政策的公开支持为其赢得了公众信任。

vocab.meaning_zh: 对……造成损害、造成负面影响（常用于形容持续的损耗）
vocab.example_en: Years of budget cuts have taken a toll on the agency's oversight capacity.
vocab.example_zh: 多年的预算削减已经损害了该机构的监管能力。

sentences.en: It’s unclear what role, if any, Jackson played in dropping the black box warning, the most serious type of federal safety warning that is reserved for drugs with severe side effects or life-threatening risks.
sentences.structure: 主干：It's unclear + 主语从句 what role ... Jackson played（It 为形式主语）/ 插入语：if any / 同位语：the most serious type of federal safety warning，其后接 that 定语从句修饰 warning
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子以 It 作形式主语开头，真正的主语是 what role Jackson played；played 的宾语就是句首的 what role。if any 是插入成分，意思是“如果有的话”，作者用它提前给“杰克逊是否参与”打了问号——这是新闻报道中避免断言、留出法律余地的常见写法。后半部分用同位语解释“黑框警告”是什么，再用 that 从句限定它的适用范围（副作用严重或有致命风险），相当于在句子内部插入了一段背景说明，让不熟悉的读者不必中断阅读去查资料。

sentences.en: But ethics experts called Jackson’s official endorsement of the warning removal “alarming” and an “obvious conflict of interest,” noting federal law prohibits government employees from participating “personally and substantially” in matters that could influence their personal finances — even making statements at a press conference or in a news release, as she also did.
sentences.structure: 主干：ethics experts called Jackson's endorsement “alarming” and an “obvious conflict of interest”（call + 宾语 + 宾补）/ 修饰：现在分词短语 noting ... 作伴随状语，说明依据 / 宾语从句：federal law prohibits ... from participating in matters / 定语从句：that could influence their personal finances / 破折号后：even making statements ... 进一步补足 participating 的范围，as she also did 为方式/比较从句
sentences.analysis_zh: 主句是简单的“主+谓+宾+宾补”结构，真正复杂的是 noting 引导的伴随状语：它为前面的指控提供法律依据，相当于“理由是……”。prohibit sb from doing sth 中，doing 的宾语是 participating in matters，matters 后面挂 that 定语从句。破折号后的 even making statements 是对 participating 的“下限延伸”——连在发布会上讲话也算参与，而 as she also did 则把这条法律标准直接扣回到杰克逊身上，使论证从抽象规则变成具体指控。这种“主句给结论＋分词状语给依据＋破折号收口”的写法，是英文评论与调查报道中常见的说理节奏。

sentences.en: Since she joined ARPA-H, the memo said, Jackson and her husband’s financial ties required her to recuse herself from “a significant portion” of her duties, including discussions about funding awarded by her agency.
sentences.structure: 主干：Jackson and her husband's financial ties required her to recuse herself from ... / 状语从句：Since she joined ARPA-H / 插入语：the memo said（引述来源）/ 介词短语：including discussions about funding awarded by her agency，修饰 her duties
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子主干是 require sb to do sth 的变体：financial ties required her to recuse herself from a significant portion of her duties。句首的 Since 从句交代时间起点，the memo said 是插入的引述标记，用来提示“以下几句话出自备忘录而非记者判断”，这是调查报道保持中立、把责任归于文件来源的手法。including ... 部分是对“相当一部分职责”的具体化，其中 awarded by her agency 是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 funding，点明被回避的正是最核心的拨款权——这也是后文说豁免“本可让她重新参与决策”的原因。

background.title: 激素替代疗法与“黑框警告”的来龙去脉
background.text_zh: 激素替代疗法（HRT）指给更年期女性补充雌激素（常联合孕激素）以缓解潮热、盗汗、骨质疏松等症状。2002年，美国一项名为“女性健康倡议”（WHI）的大型研究公布结果，称长期使用激素疗法可能提高乳腺癌、血栓和心血管事件风险，此后FDA在相关药品标签上加了“黑框警告”——这是联邦药品安全警示中最高级别，用粗黑边框突出，通常只用于风险严重甚至致命的药物。该警告导致大量女性与医生弃用HRT，处方量骤降，这一现象被学界称为“WHI后遗症”。此后二十余年，多项再分析指出当年结论对年龄分层等因素考虑不足，对较年轻、刚绝经女性的绝对风险被高估，于是近年出现“为HRT平反”的潮流，此次HHS取消黑框警告正是这一趋势的政策体现。因此文中“add up to a decade of healthy years”的说法，指的就是重新用药可能带来的健康收益。

background.title: ARPA-H、财产申报与利益冲突豁免制度
background.text_zh: ARPA-H（Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health）是拜登政府2022年设立的联邦卫生机构，模仿国防部的DARPA模式，专门资助高风险、高回报的生物医学突破性研究，2024财年预算约15亿美元，因此对生物医药和数字医疗初创公司具有巨大的资金吸引力。按照美国联邦伦理规则，行政 branch 官员须提交财产申报表（OGE Form 278e），由所在机构的伦理办公室审核并“认证”（certify）其合规；若官员持有的资产与其职责范围重叠，通常有两种处理：一是签订“回避协议”或作出回避承诺（recusal），不参与相关事项；二是由机构伦理部门签发“利益冲突豁免”（waiver），在公开披露的前提下允许其参与。豁免须依法公告，政府伦理办公室（OGE）会公开列出获豁免者。若申报表长期无法认证，机构可请监察长（inspector general）介入调查，这也是本文追问的关键点。

title_en: “Peak Greenwashing”: Two Bills in Congress Endorse Misleading Recycling Claims
excerpt_en: The post “Peak Greenwashing”: Two Bills in Congress Endorse Misleading Recycling Claims appeared first on ProPublica.
body_en: Illustration by Shoshana Gordon/ProPublica The plastics industry spent decades convincing consumers that throwing used products stamped with the “chasing arrows” symbol into a curbside bin meant they would be recycled.

Now, amid growing awareness that many of those items never get reprocessed, the industry is championing a pair of proposals in Congress that would give misleading recycling claims the support of federal law.
On the surface, the two bipartisan House bills promise transparency for consumers by establishing national standards for recycling and recycled content labels.

But the legislation — promoted by oil, chemical and packaging companies that spend millions of dollars lobbying Congress each year — would forbid states from setting stricter requirements. That would neutralize efforts like California’s “truth in labeling” law, which bans the chasing arrow symbol on plastic products that contain toxic chemicals or that can’t realistically be recycled.

One of the measures would endorse a controversial form of “mass balance” accounting that allows companies to claim a product contains recycled content when virtually none of it came from reprocessed plastic. Two years ago, a ProPublica investigation exposed the misleading, mathematical sleight of hand used in that type of mass balance, which the Biden administration subsequently prohibited for specific products.

Both bills, which have gained momentum and could face a full House vote after the midterm elections, “are peak greenwashing,” Rachel Fullmer, a staff attorney on toxics and environmental health at the Natural Resources Defense Council, said in an email. They “champion deceptive, anti-consumer policies which would result in an increase in plastic production and plastic waste incineration, all while hiding behind the false brand of ‘recycling.’”
Experts say the best solution to the plastics crisis wreaking havoc on human health and the environment is to make and use less of the material; recycling remains a marginal solution at best.

The bills tackle a growing threat to the industry, as several states have proposed or passed laws that require manufacturers to more honestly acknowledge the challenges of recycling plastic. Those measures could force companies to spend money changing their packaging or labels.
The Consumer Brands Association, which represents the packaged goods industry including Amazon, PepsiCo and Land O’Lakes, praised the House bills.

These proposals “work in tandem to reduce consumer confusion and plastic waste while providing much-needed clarity to support new domestic innovations and investments,” the organization wrote to the leaders of the House Energy and Commerce Committee in July. They “demonstrate that consumer protection and recycling-focused efforts go hand-in-hand with promoting affordability and manufacturing investments, and we strongly encourage your support for both bills.”

The association spent $2.4 million in the first half of 2026 lobbying on these bills and other issues, according to data from OpenSecrets. In September, the two recycling bills cleared the House committee.
Five Democratic House members, including three from Texas, are among the 13 co-sponsors of the bill that endorses mass balance accounting. The other has 19 co-sponsors, including one Democrat.
A few weeks ago, Sen. John Curtis, a Utah Republican, introduced the mass balance bill in the Senate; it currently has no other co-sponsors.

Sheen of Recyclability Consumers have long been confused by the chasing arrows symbol on many plastic containers. The label was created in 1970 to encourage paper recycling. The plastics industry began placing it on its products in the 1980s to quell public outrage over plastic pollution.

The symbol gave plastic the sheen of recyclability, even though most items cannot be reprocessed due to economic or technical barriers. The Environmental Protection Agency estimated that 8.7% of U.S. plastic waste was recycled in 2018; the rest ended up in landfills or was incinerated. In 2019, the Department of Energy estimated the national plastic recycling rate at 5%.

In recent years, the plastics industry has touted the promise of chemical recycling, a set of costly, often polluting technologies that break plastic into its molecular building blocks. Theoretically, these processes could take the most stubborn, unrecyclable plastics, like grocery store bags or string cheese wrappers, and rebuild them into new products.
Take ExxonMobil’s chemical recycling plant in Baytown, Texas. It uses oil refinery equipment to heat up the plastic and transform it into different chemical compounds.

Lee Zeldin, the EPA administrator, visited the Baytown plant last year. He later appeared in a promotional video, calling the facility a “proof of concept” for chemical recycling that could inspire “this entire country.”

But only 8% of the plastic waste processed by ExxonMobil gets transformed into new plastic, according to the California attorney general’s office, which sued the company in 2024 over “deceptively” promoting chemical recycling as an environmental solution. The other 92% mostly becomes fuel, which is burned rather than made into plastic products.
Citing internal company records, the lawsuit states that the recycled plastic is so heavily diluted with new plastic, the resulting products contain less than 0.1% recycled content.

In response, the company said in a court filing that while the state of California may not believe ExxonMobil’s recycling technologies are sufficient to solve the plastic waste crisis, “ExxonMobil did not assume liability for global pollution by innovating solutions to the problem.”

The company has marketed its chemically recycled products as containing “30% ISCC PLUS certified-circular” content, a technical term that could easily be misinterpreted as meaning 30% recycled material. That label is possible through a specific type of mass balance, which allows companies to claim credit in a new plastic product for the recycled molecules going into other things made in the chemical recycling process. Manufacturers can inflate the reported recycledness, or “circularity,” of the more lucrative products like plastic, while reducing the advertised recycled content of less valuable products.

enrich.title_zh: “登峰造极的洗绿”：国会两项法案为误导性回收声明背书
enrich.summary_zh: 塑料行业数十年来用“追逐箭头”标志让消费者相信塑料会被回收。如今多州立法要求诚实标注，行业转而推动国会两项两党法案：统一标签标准、禁止各州制定更严规定，并认可“质量平衡”核算，使几乎不含再生塑料的产品也能宣称含再生材料。环保组织斥之为“登峰造极的洗绿”，文章并以埃克森美孚贝敦工厂为例，说明化学回收的实际转化率极低。

paragraphs.en: Illustration by Shoshana Gordon/ProPublica The plastics industry spent decades convincing consumers that throwing used products stamped with the “chasing arrows” symbol into a curbside bin meant they would be recycled.
paragraphs.zh: （插图：Shoshana Gordon/ProPublica）几十年来，塑料行业一直在让消费者相信：只要把印有“追逐箭头”标志的用过的塑料制品扔进路边的回收桶，它们就会被回收利用。

paragraphs.en: Now, amid growing awareness that many of those items never get reprocessed, the industry is championing a pair of proposals in Congress that would give misleading recycling claims the support of federal law.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，随着越来越多的人意识到许多这类物品根本不会被再加工，该行业正在国会力推两项提案，这些提案将使误导性的回收声明获得联邦法律的支持。

paragraphs.en: On the surface, the two bipartisan House bills promise transparency for consumers by establishing national standards for recycling and recycled content labels.
paragraphs.zh: 从表面上看，这两项获两党支持的众议院法案承诺，通过为回收标签和再生含量标签制定全国统一标准，为消费者带来透明度。

paragraphs.en: But the legislation — promoted by oil, chemical and packaging companies that spend millions of dollars lobbying Congress each year — would forbid states from setting stricter requirements. That would neutralize efforts like California’s “truth in labeling” law, which bans the chasing arrow symbol on plastic products that contain toxic chemicals or that can’t realistically be recycled.
paragraphs.zh: 但这些立法——由每年花费数百万美元游说国会的石油、化工和包装企业推动——将禁止各州制定更严格的要求。这会使加州“标签真实性”法之类的努力失效；该法禁止在含有有毒化学品或实际上无法回收的塑料制品上使用追逐箭头标志。

paragraphs.en: One of the measures would endorse a controversial form of “mass balance” accounting that allows companies to claim a product contains recycled content when virtually none of it came from reprocessed plastic. Two years ago, a ProPublica investigation exposed the misleading, mathematical sleight of hand used in that type of mass balance, which the Biden administration subsequently prohibited for specific products.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一项措施将认可一种有争议的“质量平衡”核算方式，它允许企业宣称某产品含有再生材料，而实际上其中几乎没有来自再加工塑料的成分。两年前，ProPublica 的一项调查揭露了这类质量平衡中所使用的误导性“数学戏法”，拜登政府随后禁止在特定产品上使用这种做法。

paragraphs.en: Both bills, which have gained momentum and could face a full House vote after the midterm elections, “are peak greenwashing,” Rachel Fullmer, a staff attorney on toxics and environmental health at the Natural Resources Defense Council, said in an email. They “champion deceptive, anti-consumer policies which would result in an increase in plastic production and plastic waste incineration, all while hiding behind the false brand of ‘recycling.’”
paragraphs.zh: 这两项法案势头渐盛，可能在中期选举后提交众议院全体表决。自然资源保护委员会（NRDC）负责有毒物质与环境健康的专职律师雷切尔·富尔默在电子邮件中说，它们“是登峰造极的洗绿”。它们“拥护欺骗性的、反消费者的政策，将导致塑料产量和塑料垃圾焚烧量的增加，同时却躲在‘回收’这一虚假招牌背后”。

paragraphs.en: Experts say the best solution to the plastics crisis wreaking havoc on human health and the environment is to make and use less of the material; recycling remains a marginal solution at best.
paragraphs.zh: 专家表示，对于这场正在严重损害人类健康和环境的塑料危机，最好的解决办法是少生产、少使用塑料；回收充其量只是一个边缘性的解决方案。

paragraphs.en: The bills tackle a growing threat to the industry, as several states have proposed or passed laws that require manufacturers to more honestly acknowledge the challenges of recycling plastic. Those measures could force companies to spend money changing their packaging or labels.
paragraphs.zh: 这些法案应对的是该行业面临的日益严重的威胁：已有若干州提出或通过了法律，要求制造商更诚实地说明塑料回收面临的困难。这些措施可能迫使企业花钱更换包装或标签。

paragraphs.en: The Consumer Brands Association, which represents the packaged goods industry including Amazon, PepsiCo and Land O’Lakes, praised the House bills.
paragraphs.zh: 代表包装消费品行业的“消费者品牌协会”（成员包括亚马逊、百事公司和 Land O’Lakes）对这两项众议院法案表示赞赏。

paragraphs.en: These proposals “work in tandem to reduce consumer confusion and plastic waste while providing much-needed clarity to support new domestic innovations and investments,” the organization wrote to the leaders of the House Energy and Commerce Committee in July. They “demonstrate that consumer protection and recycling-focused efforts go hand-in-hand with promoting affordability and manufacturing investments, and we strongly encourage your support for both bills.”
paragraphs.zh: 该组织在7月致信众议院能源和商业委员会领导人时写道，这些提案“协同作用，可以减少消费者的困惑和塑料垃圾，同时提供亟需的明确性，以支持美国国内的新创新和新投资”。它们“表明，消费者保护和以回收为核心的努力，与提升可负担性、促进制造业投资是齐头并进的，我们强烈呼吁你们支持这两项法案”。

paragraphs.en: The association spent $2.4 million in the first half of 2026 lobbying on these bills and other issues, according to data from OpenSecrets. In September, the two recycling bills cleared the House committee.
paragraphs.zh: 根据 OpenSecrets 的数据，该协会在2026年上半年就这些法案及其他议题花费了240万美元用于游说。今年9月，这两项回收法案通过了众议院委员会的审议。

paragraphs.en: Five Democratic House members, including three from Texas, are among the 13 co-sponsors of the bill that endorses mass balance accounting. The other has 19 co-sponsors, including one Democrat.
paragraphs.zh: 在认可质量平衡核算的那项法案的13名共同提案人中，有5名民主党众议员，其中3人来自得克萨斯州。另一项法案有19名共同提案人，其中包括1名民主党人。

paragraphs.en: A few weeks ago, Sen. John Curtis, a Utah Republican, introduced the mass balance bill in the Senate; it currently has no other co-sponsors.
paragraphs.zh: 几周前，犹他州共和党参议员约翰·柯蒂斯在参议院提出了质量平衡法案；目前该法案没有其他共同提案人。

paragraphs.en: Sheen of Recyclability Consumers have long been confused by the chasing arrows symbol on many plastic containers. The label was created in 1970 to encourage paper recycling. The plastics industry began placing it on its products in the 1980s to quell public outrage over plastic pollution.
paragraphs.zh: 可回收的“光环” 长期以来，消费者对许多塑料容器上的追逐箭头标志感到困惑。这个标志于1970年创立，初衷是鼓励纸张回收。20世纪80年代，塑料行业开始把它印在自己的产品上，以平息公众对塑料污染的愤怒。

paragraphs.en: The symbol gave plastic the sheen of recyclability, even though most items cannot be reprocessed due to economic or technical barriers. The Environmental Protection Agency estimated that 8.7% of U.S. plastic waste was recycled in 2018; the rest ended up in landfills or was incinerated. In 2019, the Department of Energy estimated the national plastic recycling rate at 5%.
paragraphs.zh: 这个标志给了塑料“可回收”的光环，尽管由于经济或技术障碍，大多数物品无法被再加工。美国环保署估计，2018年美国塑料垃圾的回收率为8.7%；其余的被填埋或焚烧。2019年，美国能源部估计全国塑料回收率为5%。

paragraphs.en: In recent years, the plastics industry has touted the promise of chemical recycling, a set of costly, often polluting technologies that break plastic into its molecular building blocks. Theoretically, these processes could take the most stubborn, unrecyclable plastics, like grocery store bags or string cheese wrappers, and rebuild them into new products.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，塑料行业一直在吹捧“化学回收”的前景。这是一组成本高昂、往往会造成污染的技术，能把塑料分解成分子构件。理论上，这些工艺可以把最难处理、无法回收的塑料（如超市购物袋或奶酪棒包装）重新制成新产品。

paragraphs.en: Take ExxonMobil’s chemical recycling plant in Baytown, Texas. It uses oil refinery equipment to heat up the plastic and transform it into different chemical compounds.
paragraphs.zh: 以埃克森美孚位于得克萨斯州贝敦的化学回收工厂为例。它使用炼油设备加热塑料，将其转化为不同的化合物。

paragraphs.en: Lee Zeldin, the EPA administrator, visited the Baytown plant last year. He later appeared in a promotional video, calling the facility a “proof of concept” for chemical recycling that could inspire “this entire country.”
paragraphs.zh: 美国环保署署长李·泽尔丁去年参观了贝敦工厂。他后来出现在一段宣传视频中，称该设施是化学回收的“概念验证”，可以激励“整个国家”。

paragraphs.en: But only 8% of the plastic waste processed by ExxonMobil gets transformed into new plastic, according to the California attorney general’s office, which sued the company in 2024 over “deceptively” promoting chemical recycling as an environmental solution. The other 92% mostly becomes fuel, which is burned rather than made into plastic products.
paragraphs.zh: 但根据加州总检察长办公室的说法，埃克森美孚处理的塑料垃圾中只有8%被转化成新塑料。该办公室于2024年起诉该公司，指其“欺骗性地”将化学回收宣传为一种环保解决方案。其余92%大多变成燃料，被烧掉，而不是制成塑料制品。

paragraphs.en: Citing internal company records, the lawsuit states that the recycled plastic is so heavily diluted with new plastic, the resulting products contain less than 0.1% recycled content.
paragraphs.zh: 该诉讼援引公司内部记录称，再生塑料被新塑料稀释得太厉害，最终产品中的再生含量不足0.1%。

paragraphs.en: In response, the company said in a court filing that while the state of California may not believe ExxonMobil’s recycling technologies are sufficient to solve the plastic waste crisis, “ExxonMobil did not assume liability for global pollution by innovating solutions to the problem.”
paragraphs.zh: 作为回应，该公司在法庭文件中表示，尽管加州可能认为埃克森美孚的回收技术不足以解决塑料垃圾危机，“埃克森美孚并没有因为创新解决方案而承担全球污染的责任”。

paragraphs.en: The company has marketed its chemically recycled products as containing “30% ISCC PLUS certified-circular” content, a technical term that could easily be misinterpreted as meaning 30% recycled material. That label is possible through a specific type of mass balance, which allows companies to claim credit in a new plastic product for the recycled molecules going into other things made in the chemical recycling process. Manufacturers can inflate the reported recycledness, or “circularity,” of the more lucrative products like plastic, while reducing the advertised recycled content of less valuable products.
paragraphs.zh: 该公司在推销其化学回收产品时称其含有“30% ISCC PLUS 认证循环”成分——这是一个很容易被误读为“30%再生材料”的技术术语。这种标注之所以可行，靠的是一种特定类型的质量平衡，它允许企业把进入化学回收过程中其他产品的再生分子，记到一款新塑料产品的账上。制造商可以抬高塑料等利润更高的产品所报告的“再生度”（即“循环性”），同时压低价值较低产品所标示的再生含量。

vocab.meaning_zh: “洗绿”“绿色粉饰”，指企业以环保为名进行实质虚假或夸大的宣传
vocab.example_en: Critics called the ad campaign pure greenwashing.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者称这场广告宣传纯粹是“洗绿”。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）大力支持、力挺、倡导（某项主张或法案）
vocab.example_en: Several senators have championed the bill for years.
vocab.example_zh: 几位参议员多年来一直在力挺这项法案。

vocab.meaning_zh: 两党的、两党共同支持的（美国政治报道中的高频词）
vocab.example_en: The measure enjoys broad bipartisan support.
vocab.example_zh: 这项措施获得了广泛的两党支持。

vocab.meaning_zh: 使失效、抵消（此处指用联邦法律架空虚州一级的更严规定）
vocab.example_en: The new rule would neutralize state-level protections.
vocab.example_zh: 新规将使州一级的保护措施形同虚设。

vocab.meaning_zh: “质量平衡”，一种核算方法：把混合生产流程中的再生原料按账面比例分配到产品上，而非按物理含量计算
vocab.example_en: Under mass balance, a bottle may be labeled recycled even if it contains no recycled plastic.
vocab.example_zh: 在质量平衡核算下，一个瓶子即使不含再生塑料，也可能被标为“再生”。

vocab.meaning_zh: （字面）戏法、手法；（喻）障眼法、欺骗性的小把戏
vocab.example_en: The accounting trick was a statistical sleight of hand.
vocab.example_zh: 这种会计手法是一种统计上的障眼法。

vocab.meaning_zh: 对……造成严重破坏（外刊气候与环境报道的固定搭配）
vocab.example_en: Extreme heat is wreaking havoc on crops across the region.
vocab.example_zh: 极端高温正在对该地区各地的农作物造成严重破坏。

vocab.meaning_zh: 边缘的、微不足道的（此处强调回收作用极其有限）
vocab.example_en: Recycling plays only a marginal role in cutting emissions.
vocab.example_zh: 回收在减排中只起边缘性的作用。

vocab.meaning_zh: 吹捧、大肆宣扬、兜售（常含贬义，暗示言过其实）
vocab.example_en: The firm has long touted its recycling technology.
vocab.example_zh: 这家公司长期以来一直吹捧自己的回收技术。

vocab.meaning_zh: 协同地、一前一后配合地
vocab.example_en: The two policies should work in tandem.
vocab.example_zh: 这两项政策应当协同发挥作用。

sentences.en: But the legislation — promoted by oil, chemical and packaging companies that spend millions of dollars lobbying Congress each year — would forbid states from setting stricter requirements.
sentences.structure: 主干：the legislation would forbid states from setting stricter requirements；修饰：破折号之间的过去分词短语 promoted by... 作后置定语修饰 legislation，其中 that 引导定语从句修饰 companies。

sentences.en: One of the measures would endorse a controversial form of “mass balance” accounting that allows companies to claim a product contains recycled content when virtually none of it came from reprocessed plastic.
sentences.structure: 主干：One of the measures would endorse a form of accounting；修饰：that 引导定语从句修饰 accounting，从句内为 allow sb to claim (that)...；when 引导状语从句，表示“而实际上几乎……”。

sentences.en: That label is possible through a specific type of mass balance, which allows companies to claim credit in a new plastic product for the recycled molecules going into other things made in the chemical recycling process.
sentences.structure: 主干：That label is possible through a specific type of mass balance；修饰：which 引导非限制性定语从句修饰 mass balance；从句中 going into other things 是现在分词短语后置修饰 molecules，made in the chemical recycling process 是过去分词短语后置修饰 things。

background.title: “追逐箭头”标志的来历
background.text_zh: 文章反复提到的 chasing arrows（三个箭头首尾相接的三角形）并非环保认证，而是1970年由美国纸业推动设立、后由塑料行业采用的“树脂识别码”体系（1–7号）。它最初用于标示塑料种类以便分拣，本质是材料身份标签，与“能否被本地回收”无关。塑料行业在1980年代把它大规模印上包装，客观上让公众把“有这个三角”等同于“可回收”。正因如此，加州等州近年立法禁止在明知无法回收或含有毒物质的产品上使用该标志——这也正是文中两项联邦法案想要“联邦优先”掉的对象。

background.title: 质量平衡与 ISCC PLUS 认证
background.text_zh: 质量平衡（mass balance）本是化工与可持续认证领域的核算方法：当再生原料与原生原料在同一条生产线上混合时，按台账比例把“再生产量”分配到产品上，而不要求物理隔离。问题在于它允许“簿记式”而非“物理式”的再生含量声明，企业可以把再生分子的额度挪给利润最高的那几款产品。ISCC PLUS 是国际可持续性与碳认证体系，常以“certified-circular”字样出现在包装上，普通消费者很难分辨其含义与“30% 再生材料”的差别。文中加州诉埃克森美孚案（2024年提起）与拜登政府时期对特定产品此类声明的限制，都源于这一争议。

title_en: Meet ProPublica’s 2026 Class of Emerging Reporters
excerpt_en: The post Meet ProPublica’s 2026 Class of Emerging Reporters appeared first on ProPublica.
body_en: ProPublica’s Emerging Reporters Program provides support and mentorships to college students who are pursuing careers in investigative journalism and need additional training and financial support to help advance their goals.

Participants receive a $9,000 stipend, a trip to the annual NICAR investigative journalism conference, occasional training and presentations by speakers. They’ll also be paired one-on-one with ProPublica journalists who can help counsel them on stories, build their connections in the industry and expose them to the varied paths that careers in investigative journalism can take. Past Emerging Reporters have gone on to work at The New York Times, The Associated Press, Fresnoland, Capital B, The Tributary and other outlets.

Our goal is to encourage the next generation of journalists who seek to shine a light on abuses of power and produce stories with moral force that provoke change. In choosing the class, we look for students who demonstrate an early dedication to journalism as a career, through internships, work at local news outlets or work at campus publications. And where those opportunities — which are often unpaid — aren’t accessible, we look for other ways the student has shown an eagerness and a drive to learn the craft.
This year’s class of exceptional student journalists are from schools in Illinois, Texas, Nebraska, Iowa and New York.

Annisyn Krebs-Carr (she/her) Courtesy of Annisyn Krebs-Carr Annisyn Krebs-Carr is a senior at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign studying journalism and animal sciences. She is a reporter for Illinois Public Media Student Newsroom, where she reports on the ongoing housing crisis in Champaign-Urbana. Previously, she served as the arts and entertainment editor at The Daily Illini, the independent newspaper at the university. She is now the managing editor and oversees content produced by the entire newsroom. In 2026, she interned for St. Louis Public Radio and formed relationships with the investigative reporters at NPR’s Midwest Newsroom. This is where she developed a deeper appreciation for investigative journalism. As she continues her journalism career, she wants to focus on how the criminal justice system has failed, and continues to fail, Black people. She also wants to explore how environmental racism has impacted lower-income communities. After graduation, she hopes to work in a public media newsroom and report on local stories while honing her investigative journalism skills. Long term, Annisyn hopes to build a dedicated career as an investigative journalist in public media.

Jessica Meza (she/her) Courtesy of Jessica Meza Jessica Meza is a senior at the University of Nebraska, Lincoln studying journalism, advertising and public relations. Jessica works across mediums, including in data visualizations, video, print and social media, with an emphasis on audio reporting. Jessica hopes to begin her career in investigative, in-depth reporting, focusing on marginalized communities. She hopes to use her reporting to amplify the voice of people facing hidden injustices in her community. Other interests include housing, immigration and food reporting. Jessica currently works at Nebraska Public Media as a reporting intern. She previously interned at NPR’s Midwest Newsroom and, as the Hortencia Zavala Foundation intern, wrote for The Fulcrum and the Latino News Network. In 2025, she was part of the team at Nebraska News Service that was awarded a regional Society of Professional Journalists Mark of Excellence Award for its investigative project on missing and murdered marginalized women.

Lajward Zahra (she/her) Courtesy of Lajward Zahra Lajward Zahra is a senior English major at Rice University in Houston, originally from El Paso, Texas. Her reporting focuses on politics, immigration and the environment, particularly in Texas. She is a 2026 writing fellow at The Nation and has written for the magazine since 2023. She previously interned with the Houston Chronicle editorial board in summer 2025, reporting and writing on local and state politics, including the Texas Republican Party convention, among other issues. Lajward’s freelance work has also appeared in publications including The American Prospect, Teen Vogue, Business Insider, Rewire News Group and Scalawag. She was a 2024 Asian American Journalists Association Voices fellow.

Thai Theodoro (she/her) Courtesy of Thai Theodoro Originally from Brazil, Thai Theodoro studies political science with a concentration in Latin American studies at Grinnell College in Iowa. Now in her senior year, she is the managing editor of The Scarlet & Black, Grinnell’s independent student newspaper. Thai has interned at The Boston Globe, the Des Moines Register and the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, and her reporting has been published in dozens of newspapers across the country. She is a member of the New York Times Corps and a former participant in the National Association of Hispanic Journalists’ Student Project. Thai is passionate about telling untold stories, pursuing investigative reporting with the power to challenge the status quo, using the three languages she speaks to reach underrepresented communities, and, of course, writing the occasional quirky story.

Tsehai Alfred (she/her) Courtesy of Tsehai Alfred Tsehai Alfred is a senior at Columbia University studying English. She is the 150th editor-in-chief and president of the Columbia Daily Spectator, the campus newspaper, and is also an intern on CNN’s criminal justice team. Over the summer, she was a Dow Jones News Fund intern at VTDigger, an accountability-focused newsroom in Vermont, investigating the troubled integration of AI into healthcare, a struggling dairy farming industry, and soaring police use-of-force payouts. Previously, she has interned at City & State New York, covering the 2025 mayoral race and city council; at PBS News as a Gwen Ifill Journalism Fellow; and at her local news outlet, the Virgin Islands Consortium. Her reporting interests include local government, economic inequality, and political and corporate accountability.

enrich.title_zh: 走近 ProPublica 2026 届“新锐记者”入选者
enrich.summary_zh: ProPublica 公布 2026 年“新锐记者计划”入选名单：该计划为学生记者提供 9000 美元津贴、参加 NICAR 调查报道年会的机会，以及与 ProPublica 记者一对一的导师指导。文章随后逐一介绍五位来自伊利诺伊、内布拉斯加、得克萨斯、艾奥瓦和纽约高校的学生，呈现他们的实习经历与报道方向。

paragraphs.en: ProPublica’s Emerging Reporters Program provides support and mentorships to college students who are pursuing careers in investigative journalism and need additional training and financial support to help advance their goals.
paragraphs.zh: ProPublica 的“新锐记者计划”为立志从事调查报道职业的在校大学生提供支持与导师指导——这些学生需要额外的培训和资金支持，以推进自己的目标。

paragraphs.en: Participants receive a $9,000 stipend, a trip to the annual NICAR investigative journalism conference, occasional training and presentations by speakers. They’ll also be paired one-on-one with ProPublica journalists who can help counsel them on stories, build their connections in the industry and expose them to the varied paths that careers in investigative journalism can take. Past Emerging Reporters have gone on to work at The New York Times, The Associated Press, Fresnoland, Capital B, The Tributary and other outlets.
paragraphs.zh: 入选者将获得 9000 美元津贴、一次前往一年一度的 NICAR 调查报道会议的机会，以及不定期的培训和嘉宾演讲。他们还会与 ProPublica 的记者一对一结对，这些记者能在选题上给予指导、帮他们拓展行业人脉，并让他们了解调查报道职业可能走的多种路径。往届“新锐记者”后来进入了《纽约时报》、美联社、Fresnoland、Capital B、The Tributary 等媒体工作。

paragraphs.en: Our goal is to encourage the next generation of journalists who seek to shine a light on abuses of power and produce stories with moral force that provoke change. In choosing the class, we look for students who demonstrate an early dedication to journalism as a career, through internships, work at local news outlets or work at campus publications. And where those opportunities — which are often unpaid — aren’t accessible, we look for other ways the student has shown an eagerness and a drive to learn the craft.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的目标是鼓励下一代记者去揭露权力滥用，写出具有道德力量、能够推动改变的故事。在遴选本届学员时，我们看重那些早早表现出把新闻当作职业志向的学生——他们通过实习、在当地媒体工作或在校内刊物工作体现了这一点。而当这些往往没有报酬的机会无法获得时，我们会从其他方面寻找学生身上表现出的、对这门手艺的渴望与干劲。

paragraphs.en: This year’s class of exceptional student journalists are from schools in Illinois, Texas, Nebraska, Iowa and New York.
paragraphs.zh: 今年这批优秀的学生记者来自伊利诺伊州、得克萨斯州、内布拉斯加州、艾奥瓦州和纽约州的学校。

paragraphs.en: Annisyn Krebs-Carr (she/her) Courtesy of Annisyn Krebs-Carr Annisyn Krebs-Carr is a senior at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign studying journalism and animal sciences. She is a reporter for Illinois Public Media Student Newsroom, where she reports on the ongoing housing crisis in Champaign-Urbana. Previously, she served as the arts and entertainment editor at The Daily Illini, the independent newspaper at the university. She is now the managing editor and oversees content produced by the entire newsroom. In 2026, she interned for St. Louis Public Radio and formed relationships with the investigative reporters at NPR’s Midwest Newsroom. This is where she developed a deeper appreciation for investigative journalism. As she continues her journalism career, she wants to focus on how the criminal justice system has failed, and continues to fail, Black people. She also wants to explore how environmental racism has impacted lower-income communities. After graduation, she hopes to work in a public media newsroom and report on local stories while honing her investigative journalism skills. Long term, Annisyn hopes to build a dedicated career as an investigative journalist in public media.
paragraphs.zh: Annisyn Krebs-Carr（她/她的代词，图片由本人提供）Annisyn Krebs-Carr 是伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校的大四学生，主修新闻学与动物科学。她是 Illinois Public Media 学生新闻编辑室的记者，报道香槟-厄巴纳地区持续发酵的住房危机。此前，她曾担任该校独立报纸《The Daily Illini》的艺术与娱乐版编辑。她现在担任执行主编，负责统筹整个编辑室生产的内容。2026 年，她在圣路易斯公共广播电台实习，并与 NPR 中西部新闻编辑室的调查记者建立了联系——正是在那里，她对调查报道有了更深的认同。在继续新闻职业道路的过程中，她想聚焦刑事司法系统如何辜负了、并仍在辜负黑人群体。她还想探究环境种族主义如何影响低收入社区。毕业后，她希望进入公共媒体新闻编辑室工作，在报道本地新闻的同时磨炼调查报道技能。长远来看，Annisyn 希望以调查记者的身份在公共媒体领域深耕自己的职业生涯。

paragraphs.en: Jessica Meza (she/her) Courtesy of Jessica Meza Jessica Meza is a senior at the University of Nebraska, Lincoln studying journalism, advertising and public relations. Jessica works across mediums, including in data visualizations, video, print and social media, with an emphasis on audio reporting. Jessica hopes to begin her career in investigative, in-depth reporting, focusing on marginalized communities. She hopes to use her reporting to amplify the voice of people facing hidden injustices in her community. Other interests include housing, immigration and food reporting. Jessica currently works at Nebraska Public Media as a reporting intern. She previously interned at NPR’s Midwest Newsroom and, as the Hortencia Zavala Foundation intern, wrote for The Fulcrum and the Latino News Network. In 2025, she was part of the team at Nebraska News Service that was awarded a regional Society of Professional Journalists Mark of Excellence Award for its investigative project on missing and murdered marginalized women.
paragraphs.zh: Jessica Meza（她/她的代词，图片由本人提供）Jessica Meza 是内布拉斯加大学林肯分校的大四学生，主修新闻学、广告与公共关系。Jessica 的工作横跨多种媒介，包括数据可视化、视频、纸媒和社交媒体，尤其侧重音频报道。她希望以调查性、深度报道起步，重点关注边缘化群体。她希望借助自己的报道，放大社区中那些遭遇隐性不公者的声音。她的其他兴趣还包括住房、移民和食品报道。Jessica 目前在内布拉斯加公共媒体担任报道实习生。她此前曾在美国国家公共电台（NPR）中西部新闻编辑室实习，并以 Hortencia Zavala 基金会实习生的身份为 The Fulcrum 和 Latino News Network 撰稿。2025 年，她参与了内布拉斯加新闻服务社的团队，该团队凭借关于失踪与遇害的边缘化女性的调查项目，获得美国职业记者协会（SPJ）地区“卓越印记奖”。

paragraphs.en: Lajward Zahra (she/her) Courtesy of Lajward Zahra Lajward Zahra is a senior English major at Rice University in Houston, originally from El Paso, Texas. Her reporting focuses on politics, immigration and the environment, particularly in Texas. She is a 2026 writing fellow at The Nation and has written for the magazine since 2023. She previously interned with the Houston Chronicle editorial board in summer 2025, reporting and writing on local and state politics, including the Texas Republican Party convention, among other issues. Lajward’s freelance work has also appeared in publications including The American Prospect, Teen Vogue, Business Insider, Rewire News Group and Scalawag. She was a 2024 Asian American Journalists Association Voices fellow.
paragraphs.zh: Lajward Zahra（她/她的代词，图片由本人提供）Lajward Zahra 是休斯敦莱斯大学英语专业的大四学生，原籍得克萨斯州埃尔帕索。她的报道聚焦政治、移民和环境议题，尤其是得克萨斯州的相关议题。她是《The Nation》杂志 2026 年度写作研究员，自 2023 年起就为该刊撰稿。2025 年夏天，她在《休斯敦纪事报》社论版实习，就地方和州级政治（包括得州共和党代表大会等议题）进行采访和写作。Lajward 的自由撰稿作品还刊登在《The American Prospect》《Teen Vogue》《Business Insider》、Rewire News Group 和《Scalawag》等刊物上。她曾是美国亚裔记者协会 2024 年度的“Voices”研究员。

paragraphs.en: Thai Theodoro (she/her) Courtesy of Thai Theodoro Originally from Brazil, Thai Theodoro studies political science with a concentration in Latin American studies at Grinnell College in Iowa. Now in her senior year, she is the managing editor of The Scarlet & Black, Grinnell’s independent student newspaper. Thai has interned at The Boston Globe, the Des Moines Register and the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, and her reporting has been published in dozens of newspapers across the country. She is a member of the New York Times Corps and a former participant in the National Association of Hispanic Journalists’ Student Project. Thai is passionate about telling untold stories, pursuing investigative reporting with the power to challenge the status quo, using the three languages she speaks to reach underrepresented communities, and, of course, writing the occasional quirky story.
paragraphs.zh: Thai Theodoro（她/她的代词，图片由本人提供）Thai Theodoro 原籍巴西，在艾奥瓦州格林内尔学院主修政治学，专业方向为拉美研究。她目前读大四，是格林内尔学院的独立学生报纸《The Scarlet & Black》的执行主编。Thai 曾在《波士顿环球报》《得梅因纪事报》和《匹兹堡邮报》实习，她的报道已刊登在全美数十家报纸上。她是《纽约时报》Corps 项目成员，也曾参与全国拉美裔记者协会的学生项目。Thai 热衷于讲述未被讲述的故事，从事能够挑战现状的调查报道，用她会说的三种语言触达代表性不足的社群，当然，也乐于偶尔写写古怪有趣的小报道。

paragraphs.en: Tsehai Alfred (she/her) Courtesy of Tsehai Alfred Tsehai Alfred is a senior at Columbia University studying English. She is the 150th editor-in-chief and president of the Columbia Daily Spectator, the campus newspaper, and is also an intern on CNN’s criminal justice team. Over the summer, she was a Dow Jones News Fund intern at VTDigger, an accountability-focused newsroom in Vermont, investigating the troubled integration of AI into healthcare, a struggling dairy farming industry, and soaring police use-of-force payouts. Previously, she has interned at City & State New York, covering the 2025 mayoral race and city council; at PBS News as a Gwen Ifill Journalism Fellow; and at her local news outlet, the Virgin Islands Consortium. Her reporting interests include local government, economic inequality, and political and corporate accountability.
paragraphs.zh: Tsehai Alfred（她/她的代词，图片由本人提供）Tsehai Alfred 是哥伦比亚大学英语专业的大四学生。她是校园报纸《哥伦比亚每日观察家》第 150 任主编兼社长，同时是 CNN 刑事司法团队的实习生。去年夏天，她在佛蒙特州以问责报道见长的新闻机构 VTDigger 担任道琼斯新闻基金实习生，调查了人工智能融入医疗体系的重重困境、举步维艰的乳品业，以及大幅攀升的警方使用武力赔偿支出。此前，她曾在《City & State New York》实习，报道 2025 年市长选举和市议会；在 PBS News 担任 Gwen Ifill 新闻研究员；还在家乡媒体 Virgin Islands Consortium 实习过。她的报道兴趣包括地方政府、经济不平等，以及政治与企业的问责。

vocab.meaning_zh: （给实习生、研究员等的）津贴，补助金
vocab.example_en: Participants receive a $9,000 stipend to cover living costs during the program.
vocab.example_zh: 参与者可获得 9000 美元津贴，用于支付项目期间的生活开销。

vocab.meaning_zh: 调查报道，调查性新闻（通过长期查证揭露权力滥用、腐败等问题）
vocab.example_en: She built her career in investigative journalism, exposing corruption in local government.
vocab.example_zh: 她的职业生涯扎根于调查报道，专门揭露地方政府的腐败。

vocab.meaning_zh: 揭示，使……曝光（外刊高频比喻，指把隐蔽的问题摆到公众面前）
vocab.example_en: The documentary shines a light on abuses inside the prison system.
vocab.example_zh: 这部纪录片揭露了监狱系统内部的种种弊端。

vocab.meaning_zh: 道德力量（指报道靠道义感召而非强制力推动改变）
vocab.example_en: The story carried a moral force that no statistics could match.
vocab.example_zh: 这篇报道所蕴含的道德力量，是任何统计数据都无法比拟的。

vocab.meaning_zh: （新闻等行业的）手艺，专业本领；此处指新闻采写的技艺
vocab.example_en: Young reporters need time to learn the craft before they chase big stories.
vocab.example_zh: 年轻记者在追大新闻之前，需要时间学习这门手艺。

vocab.meaning_zh: 磨炼，打磨（技能），使日益精进
vocab.example_en: She spent two years honing her data-reporting skills at a local paper.
vocab.example_zh: 她在一家地方报纸花了两年时间打磨自己的数据报道技能。

vocab.meaning_zh: 放大，让（声音、诉求）被更多人听见；增强
vocab.example_en: The project aims to amplify voices that rarely make it into the news.
vocab.example_zh: 该项目旨在让那些很少出现在新闻里的声音被更多人听见。

vocab.meaning_zh: 被边缘化的，处于社会弱势地位的
vocab.example_en: She reports on marginalized communities that other outlets overlook.
vocab.example_zh: 她报道的是其他媒体所忽视的边缘化群体。

vocab.meaning_zh: 现状，既有格局（常与 challenge / maintain 搭配）
vocab.example_en: Investigative reporting often means challenging the status quo.
vocab.example_zh: 调查报道往往意味着挑战现状。

vocab.meaning_zh: 问责，责任追究（新闻语境中指追究权力机构的责任）
vocab.example_en: The newsroom is known for its accountability journalism on state agencies.
vocab.example_zh: 这家新闻机构以对州政府机构进行问责报道而闻名。

sentences.en: They’ll also be paired one-on-one with ProPublica journalists who can help counsel them on stories, build their connections in the industry and expose them to the varied paths that careers in investigative journalism can take.
sentences.structure: 主干：They will be paired with ProPublica journalists（被动句，one-on-one 作状语）／修饰一：who can help counsel..., build..., and expose... 为定语从句，三个动词并列，共用 help 后的宾语 them（即 help counsel them / help build their connections / help expose them）／修饰二：that careers in investigative journalism can take 为定语从句修饰 the varied paths。
sentences.analysis_zh: 全句骨架很短，只有“他们会被安排与记者结对”，信息量靠后面的定语从句层层展开。注意 help 后面接了三个并列的不带 to 的不定式（counsel / build / expose），这是英语里 help 的常见用法，阅读时要意识到这三件事都是导师要做的。结尾 the varied paths that careers can take 中，paths 是 take a path（走某条路）的搭配，定语从句把“职业路径”具体化。这种“主干短、修饰长”的写法在外刊介绍项目时很常见，先给结论再补细节。

sentences.en: Our goal is to encourage the next generation of journalists who seek to shine a light on abuses of power and produce stories with moral force that provoke change.
sentences.structure: 主干：Our goal is to encourage the next generation of journalists（表语为不定式）／修饰一：who seek to shine a light on... and produce... 为定语从句修饰 journalists，内部两个不定式并列／修饰二：with moral force 为介词短语修饰 stories；that provoke change 为定语从句，修饰 stories（而非 moral force）。
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子看似很长，主干其实只有“我们的目标是鼓励下一代记者”。两个定语从句分别锁定“什么样的记者”和“什么样的报道”，形成层层收窄的效果。理解的关键是 that provoke change 的先行词：从语义看，能“推动改变”的是 stories（报道），不是 moral force，因此它挂在 stories 后面，与 with moral force 一起构成对 stories 的双重修饰。这种连续后置修饰在英文里可以无限延长，翻译时中文要拆成分句才顺。

sentences.en: And where those opportunities — which are often unpaid — aren’t accessible, we look for other ways the student has shown an eagerness and a drive to learn the craft.
sentences.structure: 主干：we look for other ways（主句在后半句）／修饰一：where... aren’t accessible 为条件状语从句，相当于 if those opportunities aren’t accessible／修饰二：破折号中的 which are often unpaid 为插入的定语从句，修饰 those opportunities／修饰三：the student has shown... 为省略了关系词的定语从句修饰 ways（ways [that] the student has shown...）。
sentences.analysis_zh: where 在这里不是“哪里”，而是引出条件，相当于“在……无法获得的情况下”，把它读成 if 即可。破折号插入语是补充说明，可先跳过以抓主干。最后 ways 后面的从句省略了 that/in which，因为先行词是 ways，这种省略在口语化书面语里很常见。整句的论证逻辑是：先承认现实（实习往往无薪、并非人人可及），再说明评选标准会因此调整，体现出一种务实的公平考量。

background.title: ProPublica 与“新锐记者计划”
background.text_zh: ProPublica 是美国一家非营利调查报道机构，2007 年成立，总部在纽约，靠基金会资助与捐赠运营，其报道免费提供给合作媒体转载。它多次获得普利策奖，以“问责式新闻”（accountability journalism）著称。Emerging Reporters Program 是该机构面向本科生的人才培养项目，每年遴选数名有志于调查报道的学生，提供津贴、会议机会和一对一导师，目的是在新闻业实习普遍低薪甚至无薪的情况下，降低入行门槛。文中提到的往届学员去向（《纽约时报》、美联社等）正是该项目用来证明成效的方式。

background.title: NICAR 会议与美国调查报道生态
background.text_zh: NICAR 全称 National Institute for Computer-Assisted Reporting，隶属于 Investigative Reporters and Editors（IRE）组织，每年举办“计算机辅助报道”年会，是美国数据新闻与调查报道领域最重要的行业聚会，记者在会上交流数据抓取、可视化、数据库分析等技能——这与文中多位学生提到数据可视化、音频、跨媒介报道相呼应。此外文中出现的 SPJ（美国职业记者协会）、亚裔记者协会（AAJA）、全国拉美裔记者协会（NAHJ）、道琼斯新闻基金（Dow Jones News Fund）都是美国新闻业常见的行业协会或奖学金机构，学生记者往往通过这类项目获得第一份实习。

title_en: How Cleta Mitchell Turned Trump’s “Big Lie” Into a Movement
excerpt_en: The post How Cleta Mitchell Turned Trump’s “Big Lie” Into a Movement appeared first on ProPublica.
body_en: Photo illustration by Lisa Larson-Walker/ProPublica. Source images: Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images; Win McNamee/Getty Images. In July, not long before President Donald Trump delivered a primetime address questioning the legitimacy of American elections, the pioneering conservative election lawyer Cleta Mitchell and about two dozen of her associates logged onto a private video briefing with the White House.

Mitchell, who holds no formal position in the Trump administration, had been pivotal to Trump’s bid to challenge his loss in 2020, spearheading efforts to prove his claims of fraud and reverse his defeat in court.

After Joe Biden took office, when others abandoned the fight or scoffed as Trump clung to conspiracy theories, Mitchell doubled down, founding a grassroots organization devoted to rewriting election laws and rules to be more restrictive. Members of her group, the Election Integrity Network, were named to vital election-related positions in swing states and, later, in the second Trump administration.

The pre-speech briefing was an acknowledgment of just how consequential Mitchell and her organization had become. The White House had held similar sessions for key political players, such as governors, members of Congress and major press outlets.

Help Us Report on Key Election Issues ProPublica’s reporters are on the lookout for what’s going right and what isn’t. We’re monitoring voter suppression and interference, election observers and poll watchers, extremism tied to the election, and ICE activity at the polls. Have you seen something?

Send Us a Tip At the appointed time, the screen filled with the faces of EIN leaders and supporters, some sitting in front of digital backgrounds with the group’s logo on them. Mitchell shushed those who’d forgotten to mute and introduced John Solomon, an ally of hers who was helping prepare the speech.
Mitchell and her network hardly needed the run-through, though: Much of the speech was a compendium of allegations and conspiracy theories they had originated or spread.

Her lieutenants were thrilled to hear that the president would assert there were more than 275,000 noncitizens on state voter rolls — a since-debunked claim based on work led by one of her proteges, who occupied a top post at the Department of Homeland Security.
The speech would end with an exhortation for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, a bill requiring voters to provide documentary proof of citizenship to register, which Mitchell had helped draft.
To Seth Keshel, an EIN adviser on the call, none of it was surprising — Mitchell was in and out of the White House all the time. He’d joined her for one such meeting.
“She’s got an open door with the president,” he said.

Cleta Mitchell founded a grassroots organization, the Election Integrity Network, devoted to rewriting election laws and rules to be more restrictive. Travis Dove/The New York Times/Redux “Opposed to Honest Elections” Obtained by ProPublica No one besides Trump himself has done more than Mitchell, 76, to turn the mundane processes of how ballots are cast and counted in American elections into mortal combat.

Since Trump returned to the White House, Mitchell and her acolytes have been deeply entwined in his unprecedented bid to assert federal control over voting, an effort that has increasingly defined his second term.

Friends and enemies alike credit her with providing much of the administration’s election road map. The White House has turned to those close to her to enact the plan, appointing her associates to help lead the hunt for noncitizens on voter rolls and to reinvestigate 2020 voting irregularities.

“She has the president’s ear,” Steve Bannon, Trump’s former chief strategist and a close ally of Mitchell’s, said in a July interview. “A lot of the momentum things we’ve seen over the last six months or so come directly from Cleta’s involvement.”
To understand how Mitchell became the hand behind this transformational push, ProPublica traced her obsession with politics and elections back to its roots.
From the start, those who knew her told us, she stood out for her willingness to embrace options others wouldn’t and to do whatever it took to win.
Her relentlessness and long-term strategic vision have enabled her to outflank or outlast not only her liberal opponents, but her conservative rivals.

Much of Mitchell’s influence derives from years of groundwork she’s done to put a foundation under the so-called election-integrity movement, once dismissed as a collection of oddballs and fringe actors.
Beyond building the EIN and raising millions of dollars to fund its activities, she’s helped direct tens of millions more to like-minded policy shops, researchers, law firms and advocacy groups.

The net effect has been to make an agreed-upon set of beliefs about elections — that the 2020 presidential vote was stolen, that U.S. voting systems are rigged, that there’s rampant voting by noncitizens — a core part of conservatism.

Rick Wilson, a former Republican strategist who collaborated with Mitchell before Trump’s election and now heads the anti-Trump Lincoln Project, said she had been crucial in building the institutional infrastructure that has sustained Trump’s “big lie.”

enrich.title_zh: 克莱塔·米切尔如何把特朗普的“大谎言”变成一场运动
enrich.summary_zh: 本文梳理保守派律师克莱塔·米切尔的崛起轨迹：2020年特朗普败选后，在众人放弃时她反而加码，创立“选举诚信网络”，向摇摆州选举岗位输送人马、为限制投票的立法铺路、为“选举诚信”运动筹款筑基，最终成为特朗普第二任期推动联邦介入选举事务的幕后设计师。

paragraphs.en: Photo illustration by Lisa Larson-Walker/ProPublica. Source images: Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images; Win McNamee/Getty Images. In July, not long before President Donald Trump delivered a primetime address questioning the legitimacy of American elections, the pioneering conservative election lawyer Cleta Mitchell and about two dozen of her associates logged onto a private video briefing with the White House.
paragraphs.zh: 图片合成：Lisa Larson-Walker/ProPublica。图片来源：Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images；Win McNamee/Getty Images。今年7月，就在唐纳德·特朗普总统发表黄金时段讲话、质疑美国选举的合法性之前不久，保守派选举律师中的先驱人物克莱塔·米切尔（Cleta Mitchell）和大约二十多名同伴登录了一场与白宫之间的私密视频简报会。

paragraphs.en: Mitchell, who holds no formal position in the Trump administration, had been pivotal to Trump’s bid to challenge his loss in 2020, spearheading efforts to prove his claims of fraud and reverse his defeat in court.
paragraphs.zh: 米切尔在特朗普政府中并无正式职位，但在特朗普试图挑战2020年败选结果的过程中，她发挥了关键作用，带头推动两件事：证明他所称的“舞弊”，以及在法庭上推翻他的败选结果。

paragraphs.en: After Joe Biden took office, when others abandoned the fight or scoffed as Trump clung to conspiracy theories, Mitchell doubled down, founding a grassroots organization devoted to rewriting election laws and rules to be more restrictive. Members of her group, the Election Integrity Network, were named to vital election-related positions in swing states and, later, in the second Trump administration.
paragraphs.zh: 乔·拜登就职后，当其他人放弃这场斗争、或对特朗普死抱阴谋论嗤之以鼻时，米切尔反而加码下注，创立了一个草根组织，致力于改写选举法律与规则、使之更加严苛。她这个名为“选举诚信网络”（Election Integrity Network）的组织的成员，被任命到摇摆州与选举相关的要害岗位上，后来又进入特朗普第二届政府任职。

paragraphs.en: The pre-speech briefing was an acknowledgment of just how consequential Mitchell and her organization had become. The White House had held similar sessions for key political players, such as governors, members of Congress and major press outlets.
paragraphs.zh: 这场讲话前的简报会本身就是一个印证，说明米切尔和她的组织已经变得多么举足轻重。白宫此前只为州长、国会议员和各大媒体等关键政治角色举办过类似的吹风会。

paragraphs.en: Help Us Report on Key Election Issues ProPublica’s reporters are on the lookout for what’s going right and what isn’t. We’re monitoring voter suppression and interference, election observers and poll watchers, extremism tied to the election, and ICE activity at the polls. Have you seen something?
paragraphs.zh: 【协助我们报道关键选举议题】ProPublica的记者正在留意哪些环节运转正常、哪些不正常。我们正在关注选民压制与选举干预、选举观察员与投票站监督员、与选举相关的极端主义，以及移民与海关执法局（ICE）在投票站的活动。你亲眼看到过什么情况吗？

paragraphs.en: Send Us a Tip At the appointed time, the screen filled with the faces of EIN leaders and supporters, some sitting in front of digital backgrounds with the group’s logo on them. Mitchell shushed those who’d forgotten to mute and introduced John Solomon, an ally of hers who was helping prepare the speech.
paragraphs.zh: 【向我们提供线索】约定时间一到，屏幕上挤满了EIN领导人和支持者的面孔，其中一些人身后还是印有该组织标志的虚拟背景。米切尔对那些忘了静音的人“嘘”了一声，随后介绍了她的盟友约翰·所罗门（John Solomon）——此人正在协助准备这篇讲话。

paragraphs.en: Mitchell and her network hardly needed the run-through, though: Much of the speech was a compendium of allegations and conspiracy theories they had originated or spread.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，米切尔和她的网络其实几乎用不着这次预演：讲话的大部分内容，不过是他们自己炮制或传播过的各种指控与阴谋论的汇编。

paragraphs.en: Her lieutenants were thrilled to hear that the president would assert there were more than 275,000 noncitizens on state voter rolls — a since-debunked claim based on work led by one of her proteges, who occupied a top post at the Department of Homeland Security.
paragraphs.zh: 听到总统将宣称各州选民名册上有超过27.5万名非公民，她的手下们兴奋不已——这一说法后来已被证伪，它依据的是她一位门生主导的工作，而此人当时在国土安全部担任高层职务。

paragraphs.en: The speech would end with an exhortation for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, a bill requiring voters to provide documentary proof of citizenship to register, which Mitchell had helped draft.
paragraphs.zh: 讲话最后将呼吁国会通过《拯救美国法案》（SAVE America Act）——该法案要求选民登记时提供公民身份的书面证明，米切尔曾参与起草。

paragraphs.en: To Seth Keshel, an EIN adviser on the call, none of it was surprising — Mitchell was in and out of the White House all the time. He’d joined her for one such meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 对参加这通电话会议的EIN顾问塞思·凯谢尔（Seth Keshel）来说，这一切都不足为奇——米切尔常年出入白宫。他曾陪她参加过一次这样的会议。

paragraphs.en: “She’s got an open door with the president,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “总统对她的大门始终敞开。”他说。

paragraphs.en: Cleta Mitchell founded a grassroots organization, the Election Integrity Network, devoted to rewriting election laws and rules to be more restrictive. Travis Dove/The New York Times/Redux “Opposed to Honest Elections” Obtained by ProPublica No one besides Trump himself has done more than Mitchell, 76, to turn the mundane processes of how ballots are cast and counted in American elections into mortal combat.
paragraphs.zh: 图注：克莱塔·米切尔创立了一个草根组织“选举诚信网络”，致力于改写选举法律与规则、使之更加严苛。Travis Dove/The New York Times/Redux。小标题：“反对诚实选举”。ProPublica获取。除了特朗普本人，现年76岁的米切尔比任何人都更卖力地把美国选举中投票与计票这些平淡无奇的程序，变成一场你死我活的搏斗。

paragraphs.en: Since Trump returned to the White House, Mitchell and her acolytes have been deeply entwined in his unprecedented bid to assert federal control over voting, an effort that has increasingly defined his second term.
paragraphs.zh: 自特朗普重返白宫以来，米切尔及其追随者深度卷入了他那项史无前例的主张——让联邦政府对选举拥有控制权；这一努力正日益成为他第二任期的标志性特征。

paragraphs.en: Friends and enemies alike credit her with providing much of the administration’s election road map. The White House has turned to those close to her to enact the plan, appointing her associates to help lead the hunt for noncitizens on voter rolls and to reinvestigate 2020 voting irregularities.
paragraphs.zh: 无论敌友，都认为这届政府的选举路线图很大程度上出自她手。白宫转而倚重她的亲信来落实这一计划，任命她的同僚牵头清查选民名册中的非公民，并重新调查2020年的投票异常情况。

paragraphs.en: “She has the president’s ear,” Steve Bannon, Trump’s former chief strategist and a close ally of Mitchell’s, said in a July interview. “A lot of the momentum things we’ve seen over the last six months or so come directly from Cleta’s involvement.”
paragraphs.zh: “总统听得进她的话，”特朗普前首席战略师、米切尔的亲密盟友史蒂夫·班农（Steve Bannon）在7月的一次采访中说，“过去半年左右我们看到的一连串势头，很多都直接来自克莱塔的参与。”

paragraphs.en: To understand how Mitchell became the hand behind this transformational push, ProPublica traced her obsession with politics and elections back to its roots.
paragraphs.zh: 为了弄清米切尔如何成为这场变革性行动背后的那只手，ProPublica追溯了她对政治与选举的执念的根源。

paragraphs.en: From the start, those who knew her told us, she stood out for her willingness to embrace options others wouldn’t and to do whatever it took to win.
paragraphs.zh: 认识她的人告诉我们，从一开始，她就格外显眼：她愿意采用别人不会采用的手段，为取胜不惜一切代价。

paragraphs.en: Her relentlessness and long-term strategic vision have enabled her to outflank or outlast not only her liberal opponents, but her conservative rivals.
paragraphs.zh: 她的执着与长远战略眼光，使她不仅能够包抄或熬过她的自由派对手，也能胜过保守派阵营内的竞争者。

paragraphs.en: Much of Mitchell’s influence derives from years of groundwork she’s done to put a foundation under the so-called election-integrity movement, once dismissed as a collection of oddballs and fringe actors.
paragraphs.zh: 米切尔的影响力很大程度上源于她多年打下的基础——为所谓的“选举诚信”运动筑起根基，而这场运动一度被视为一群怪人和边缘人物的拼凑而遭人轻视。

paragraphs.en: Beyond building the EIN and raising millions of dollars to fund its activities, she’s helped direct tens of millions more to like-minded policy shops, researchers, law firms and advocacy groups.
paragraphs.zh: 除了建立EIN并为其活动筹集数百万美元之外，她还协助把数千万美元引导给理念相近的政策机构、研究人员、律师事务所和倡议团体。

paragraphs.en: The net effect has been to make an agreed-upon set of beliefs about elections — that the 2020 presidential vote was stolen, that U.S. voting systems are rigged, that there’s rampant voting by noncitizens — a core part of conservatism.
paragraphs.zh: 最终效果是，一套关于选举的“共识性信念”——2020年总统选举被窃取、美国的投票系统遭操纵、非公民投票泛滥——变成了保守主义的核心组成部分。

paragraphs.en: Rick Wilson, a former Republican strategist who collaborated with Mitchell before Trump’s election and now heads the anti-Trump Lincoln Project, said she had been crucial in building the institutional infrastructure that has sustained Trump’s “big lie.”
paragraphs.zh: 前共和党战略师里克·威尔逊（Rick Wilson）曾在特朗普当选前与米切尔合作，如今领导反特朗普的“林肯计划”。他说，在搭建起支撑特朗普“大谎言”的制度性基础设施方面，她起到了至关重要的作用。

vocab.meaning_zh: （在风险已高的情况下）加码下注；变本加厉地坚持
vocab.example_en: Rather than back off after the criticism, the company doubled down on its ad campaign.
vocab.example_zh: 遭到批评后，这家公司非但没有收手，反而在广告宣传上加码投入。

vocab.meaning_zh: 带头推动，充当先锋
vocab.example_en: She spearheaded the campaign to tighten voter registration rules.
vocab.example_zh: 她带头推动了收紧选民登记规则的行动。

vocab.meaning_zh: 影响重大的，举足轻重的
vocab.example_en: It was one of the most consequential elections in the country’s history.
vocab.example_zh: 那是这个国家历史上影响最重大的选举之一。

vocab.meaning_zh: 揭穿，证伪（说法、神话）
vocab.example_en: The report debunked the claim that thousands of ballots had been forged.
vocab.example_zh: 该报告证伪了有数千张选票被伪造的说法。

vocab.meaning_zh: （正式的）呼吁，劝诫
vocab.example_en: The speech ended with an exhortation to lawmakers to act.
vocab.example_zh: 讲话以呼吁立法者采取行动作结。

vocab.meaning_zh: 预演，排练，通读一遍
vocab.example_en: We did a final run-through of the presentation the night before.
vocab.example_zh: 我们在头天晚上对演示做了一次最终彩排。

vocab.meaning_zh: 追随者，门徒（含贬义或戏谑色彩）
vocab.example_en: The senator arrived surrounded by a small group of acolytes.
vocab.example_zh: 这位参议员在一小群追随者的簇拥下到场。

vocab.meaning_zh: （迂回）包抄；在策略上智胜对手
vocab.example_en: The group outflanked its rivals by organizing at the county level.
vocab.example_zh: 该团体通过在县一级布局，在策略上绕过了对手。

vocab.meaning_zh: 边缘的，非主流的
vocab.example_en: The theory long lived on the fringe of American politics.
vocab.example_zh: 这一理论长期游走于美国政治的边缘。

vocab.meaning_zh: 选民名册（州或地方登记的合格选民名单）
vocab.example_en: States are required to maintain accurate voter rolls.
vocab.example_zh: 各州须维护准确的选民名册。

sentences.en: Mitchell, who holds no formal position in the Trump administration, had been pivotal to Trump’s bid to challenge his loss in 2020, spearheading efforts to prove his claims of fraud and reverse his defeat in court.
sentences.structure: 主干：Mitchell had been pivotal to Trump’s bid（主系表）／修饰：who holds no formal position… 非限制性定语从句修饰 Mitchell；to challenge his loss in 2020 不定式作 bid 的后置定语；spearheading… 现在分词短语作伴随状语，逻辑主语仍是 Mitchell。

sentences.en: No one besides Trump himself has done more than Mitchell, 76, to turn the mundane processes of how ballots are cast and counted in American elections into mortal combat.
sentences.structure: 主干：No one has done more than Mitchell to turn A into B／修饰：besides Trump himself 介词短语限定 no one；76 为同位语补充年龄；of how ballots are cast and counted 是介词 of + 宾语从句，修饰 processes；to turn… 不定式作状语，说明“做得更多”是指做什么。
